> For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ultimateshop.superiormc.cn/llms.txt). Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://ultimateshop.superiormc.cn/info/compatibility.md).

# 🔗Compatibility

The compatibility of plugins mainly includes hooks for **item plugins** and **economy plugins**. Unlike other plugins of the same type, we can support them regardless of their appearance. There are two methods to support them: **direct compatibility** and **indirect compatibility**.

## **Direct compatibility**

Direct compatibility refers to the use of item plugins or the economy of economic plugins directly in **ItemFormat** or **EconomyFormat**. This compatibility method is the simplest and officially supported.

### Directly supported item plugins list

* ItemsAdder
* Oraxen
* EcoItems
* EcoArmor
* MMOItems
* MythicMobs
* eco
* NeigeItems
* ExecutableItems
* Nexo
* CraftEngine

You can use ItemBridge as custom item provider which supports more custom item plugins, click [here](/format/itembridge.md) to know more.

### Directly supported economy plugins list

* PlayerPoints
* CoinsEngine
* UltraEconomy
* EcoBits
* PEconomy
* RedisEconomy
* RoyaleEconomy
* VotingPlugin

The following provides an example of directly obtaining items from the **ItemsAdder** plugin through the direct compatibility feature in **ItemFormat** and using economy from **Vault** plugin in **EconomyFormat**:

```yaml
items:
A:
price-mode: CLASSIC_ALL
product-mode: CLASSIC_ALL
products:
1:
hook-plugin: ItemsAdder # Item Format
hook-item: fishing_pack:common_fishing_bait # Item Forma
buy-prices:
1:
economy-plugin: Vault # Economy Format
amount: 5
start-apply: 0
placeholder: '&65 Coins'
```

### Directly supported protection plugins list

{% hint style="info" %}
Although the protection plugin you are using is not on this list, as long as the corresponding plugin can prevent the player from interacting with the corresponding container, UltimateShop will not trigger a sell stick, depending on how the author of the plugin you are using wrote their plugin.
{% endhint %}

If players do not have permission to open container within these protection plugins areas, UltimateShop can prevent players use sell stick in these areas.

* BentoBox
* Dominion
* GriefPrevention
* HuskTowns
* HuskClaims
* Lands
* PlotSquared
* Residence
* Towny
* WorldGuard
* SuperiorSkyblock2

### Directly supported hologram plugins list

Support create hologram to display sell chest info.

* CMI
* DecentHolograms
* FancyHolograms

## **Indirect compatibility**

Indirect compatibility refers to the flexible use of various features of plugins to enable them to associate with these plugins.

* [Save Item](/features/saved-item-item-manager.md): We told you a command called `/shop saveitem` at [Commands](/info/commands-and-permissions.md) page, we also told you can set `material` option in [Item Format](/format/itemformat-tm.md) to the save item ID you was set to use them.
* Buy Actions: We told you a option called `buy-actions` in shop configs at [Shops](/shops/shops.md) page. In [Actions](/format/action-format.md) page, we also told you we support use command in actions, so just use the give item command here, all is done.
* Give Actions: We told you this feature at [Single Things](/shops/products-config-single-thing.md) page which is very similar to **Buy Actions**. What's more, we even give you an example at that page.

### Example: Use for not supported item plugins as products

In this example, we first fill in the **ItemFormat** through the display item option to describe the item from an incompatible plugin, so that players can see what the item looks like in the menu.

In the `products` option, we use the [Custom Sell Match](/features/custom-item-match-method.md) feature, which allows us to flexibly set the rules for selling matches for this item, such as `contains-lore`, etc. Then, we use `give-actions` format to execute the item give command, so that player can obtain this item after buy.

```yaml
display-item:
material: APPLE
# You can hold the item and type command /shop generateitemformat to get the ItemFormat here.
products:
1:
# Sell Match
match-item:
contains-lore:
- 'test1'
# Buy Give Command
give-actions:
1:
multi-once: true
type: console_command
command: 'items give {player} {amount}'
2:
type: message
message: 'test message'
amount: 64
```

If you use the Paper server and the item is fixed (the items generated each time are identical), you can use the Save item function: you only need to use the `/shop saveitem` command, then use the `material` option in **ItemFormat**, and fill in the ID of the save item in this option.

### Example: Use for not supported economy plugins as prices.

In this example, we mainly flexibly implemented different types of single thing and `give-actions` and `take-actions` options, whose functions can be found on the [Products](/shops/products.md) page. Specifically, assuming the player purchases this product, the `match-placeholder` in buy options is used to determine if the player has enough economy. If it meets the `buy-prices` requirement, the player will receive an apple in `products` section and execute `take-actions` section in buy-prices section. Similarly, during selling, as the player obtains the sell price, the `give-actions` in the sell price will be executed, and therefore the player will receive economy.

{% hint style="info" %}
Require **PREMIUM** version of UltimateShop!
{% endhint %}

```yaml
products:
1:
# The product
material: APPLE
amount: 64
buy-prices:
1:
# Buy Match Placeholder
match-placeholder: '%economy_now_balance_placeholder%'
amount: 500
# Buy Take Actions
take-actions:
1:
multi-once: true
type: console_command
command: 'eco take {player} {amount}'
sell-prices:
1:
# Sell Give Actions
give-actions:
1:
multi-once: true
type: 'console_command'
command: 'eco give {player} {amount}'
amount: 500
```

## MythicChanger: Extra Item Format option

Through this hook, based on the [ItemFormat](/format/itemformat-tm.md), items can be further modified to their desired appearance.

This feature require your server must install **MythicChanger** plugin, please get it here:

**FREE:** [Click to download](https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/mythicchanger-match-and-modify-all-your-items-without-trouble-1-14-1-21.98523/)

**PREMIUM:** [Click to download](https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/mythicchanger-premium-match-and-modify-all-your-items-without-trouble-1-14-1-21.115913/)

For how to configure the `change-item` section, please read MythicChanger's wiki, [click here](https://mythicchanger.superiormc.cn/) to visit. Please note that some of the change rules require **PREMIUM version of MythicChanger, not PREMIUM version of UltimateShop**!

change-item:
set-name: '&fGood Diamond Sword'

## AdvancedEnchantments: Extra Item Format option - Premium

Through this hook, based on the [ItemFormat](/format/itemformat-tm.md), items can have custom enchantments from AdvancedmentEnchantments.

Plugin like `EcoEnchants, ExcellentEnchants` are vanilla enchants like plugin, you just need to put their enchantment ID to `enchants` option in [ItemFormat](/format/itemformat-tm.md#enchants).

You can use `plugin-enchants` option to add plugin enchants for your item.

```yaml
plugin-enchants:
PLANTER: 5 # A AdvancedEnchantments enchantment
```

## NBTAPI: Extra Item Format option - Premium

The format of this option is:

```yaml
nbt:
:
:
```

Supported NBT Type: '

* byte
* short
* int
* long
* float
* double
* string

For example:

```yaml
nbt:
string:
customNBT: 'Hello!'
int:
anotherNBTComponent.theNBTKey: 5
```

## MythicChanger: Custom Item Match

[Custom Item Match Method](/features/custom-item-match-method.md) feature requires MythicChanger.

## PlaceholderAPI: Extra placeholders

UltimateShop provides those new placeholders to PlaceholderAPI, for more info, please view [this page](/placeholders/built-in-placeholders.md#placeholderapi-support).

📦Info

🛠️Configuration files

The plugin generates the following configuration files, some of which will only be generated after you first use this feature.

datas: The location for storing plugin data files. It will only be generated without using a database. Do not modify any content here.

items: The location for storing saved item files.

languages: The location for storing language files. You can set the language file used by the plugin through the config-files.language option in the config.yml file. You can customize various messages within the plugin game through language files. For per player language, or send action bar/title/boss bar/sound, please view this page.

menus/common_menus: The location for storing common menu configuration files.

menus/shop_menu_templates: The location for storing shop menu template files.

menus/buy_more_menus: The location for storing buy more menu files.

menus/favourite_menus: The location for storing favourite menu files.

menus/search_menus: The location for storing search menu files.

menus/item_sell_menus: The location for storing item sell menu files.

Many people seem to be confused about one thing: what you open through the /shop command is a menu, not a shop. If you want to set the slot for items in the shop menu, you should set it in the configuration file of the menu.

shops: The location for storing shop configuration files.

placeholders/random_placeholders: The loaction for storing random placeholder configuration files.

placeholders/custom_placeholders: The location for storing custom placeholder configuration files.

placeholders/conditional_placeholders: The location for storing conditional placeholder configuration files.

sell_sticks: The location for storing sell stick configuration files.

config.yml file: The location for main common settings for plugins.

generated-item-format.yml file: When using the /shop generateitemformat command, we will parse the item you are holding into an ItemFormat and store the parsed ItemFormat content in this file.

minecraft-resources/<version>/: Downloaded Minecraft data, textures and language caches used by automatic menu icons and localized item names. These files are prepared automatically.

XX.txt file: The transaction record file generated by the Log Transaction feature is named using the log-transaction.file option in the config.yml file.

Legacy top-level placeholder and specialized menu folders are automatically moved into placeholders/ and menus/ when the plugin starts. If both locations contain the same file, the new file is used and the old file is preserved with a console warning for manual merging. Existing common menu files and custom subfolders in menus/ are moved into menus/common_menus/.

For Paper component ItemFormat examples and save/rebuild checks, see Component Format and Testing Paper Components.

Config.yml file content

It is recommend that you view this file at GitHub, becuase Wiki's config.yml maybe not latest. Click here to view this file on Github.

> For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ultimateshop.superiormc.cn/llms.txt). Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://ultimateshop.superiormc.cn/info/configuration-files.md).

# 🛠️Configuration files

The plugin generates the following configuration files, some of which will only be generated after you first use this feature.

* `datas`: The location for storing plugin data files. It will only be generated without using a database. Do not modify any content here.
* `items`: The location for storing saved item files.
* `languages`: The location for storing language files. You can set the language file used by the plugin through the `config-files.language` option in the `config.yml` file. You can customize various messages within the plugin game through language files. For per player language, or send action bar/title/boss bar/sound, please view [this page](/features/advanced-language-managment.md).
* `menus/common_menus`: The location for storing common menu configuration files.
* `menus/shop_menu_templates`: The location for storing shop menu template files.
* `menus/buy_more_menus`: The location for storing buy more menu files.
* `menus/favourite_menus`: The location for storing favourite menu files.
* `menus/search_menus`: The location for storing search menu files.
* `menus/item_sell_menus`: The location for storing item sell menu files.

{% hint style="info" %}
Many people seem to be confused about one thing: what you open through the `/shop` command is a menu, not a shop. If you want to set the slot for items in the shop menu, you should set it in the configuration file of the menu.
{% endhint %}

* `shops`: The location for storing shop configuration files.
* `placeholders/random_placeholders`: The loaction for storing random placeholder configuration files.
* `placeholders/custom_placeholders`: The location for storing custom placeholder configuration files.
* `placeholders/conditional_placeholders`: The location for storing conditional placeholder configuration files.
* `sell_sticks`: The location for storing sell stick configuration files.
* `config.yml` file: The location for main common settings for plugins.
* `generated-item-format.yml` file: When using the `/shop generateitemformat` command, we will parse the item you are holding into an **ItemFormat** and store the parsed **ItemFormat** content in this file.
* `minecraft-resources//`: Downloaded Minecraft data, textures and language caches used by automatic menu icons and localized item names. These files are prepared automatically.
* `XX.txt` file: The transaction record file generated by the [Log Transaction](/features/log-transaction-premium.md) feature is named using the `log-transaction.file` option in the `config.yml` file.

Legacy top-level placeholder and specialized menu folders are automatically moved into `placeholders/` and `menus/` when the plugin starts. If both locations contain the same file, the new file is used and the old file is preserved with a console warning for manual merging. Existing common menu files and custom subfolders in `menus/` are moved into `menus/common_menus/`.

For Paper component ItemFormat examples and save/rebuild checks, see [Component Format](/format/itemformat-tm/component-format.md) and [Testing Paper Components](https://github.com/ManyouTeam/UltimateShop/tree/master/docs/format/itemformat-tm/component-testing.md).

## Config.yml file content

It is recommend that you view this file at GitHub, becuase Wiki's `config.yml` maybe not **latest**. Click [here](https://github.com/PQguanfang/UltimateShop/blob/master/plugin/src/main/resources/config.yml) to view this file on **Github.**

```yaml
# UltimateShop by @PQguanfang
#
# Read the Wiki: ultimateshop.superiormc.cn

# Some options require restart the server to make effect.

debug: false

config-files:
language: en_US
# Premium version only.
```

> For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ultimateshop.superiormc.cn/llms.txt). Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://ultimateshop.superiormc.cn/info/data.md).

# 📊Data

## Data Type

UltimateShop has 2 data types, they are: Player Data and Server Data.

Player data saves player self data, like each product buy times and sell times, cooldown times, and other things.

Server data saved server total product buy times, sell times and so on. Random placeholder's data will also saved in server data.

## Save

For player data, we will auto save player data into database when player leave the server.

For server data, we will auto save server data when you are trying to stop the server normally. (Not directly close the console window, you need use /stop command in server)

Data not saved will be lost after server crash, so enable auto save feature if you don't want this.

## Auto Save

You can use auto save feature so that plugin can store plugin data periodically to avoid data loss due to server crashes. It is not recommended to store at a high frequency, as this can cause server lag. You can find the following content in `config.yml` to set this feature:

```yaml
auto-save:
enabled: true
hide-message: false
period-tick: 6000 # In ticks, 20 ticks = 1 second.
```

## Database

You can find the following content in `config.yml` to set this feature:

```yaml
database:
enabled: false
jdbc-url: "jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/ultimateshop?useSSL=false&autoReconnect=true"
jdbc-class: "com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver"
properties:
user: root
password: 123456
```

❓FAQ

Q: Player don't cost money when buy product.

A: That is simply because you give self * permission so plugin will bypass price check for you. For common player, it will work correctly.

Q: My item can not be sold in shop, but I think they are same item.

A: No, actually they have small different, but you dind't find them. The simplest way is to change the sell-methods option in config.yml from Bukkit to ItemFormat.

Q: Does the /shop command has permission?

A: Use /shop can directly open a menu called main. This is a feature called Auto Open, and you can disable it at config.yml file with menu.auto-open.enabled option. If you only want some players to be exposed to this command, you can set conditions for the menu so that only players who meet the specified conditions can open the menu. For more info, please view Menus page.

Q: Why it say condition not meet when open daily example menu?

A: That menu already has a condition, which you can find in menus/shop_menu_templates/daily-shop-menu.yml.

Q: Why can I only sell 64x (or other amunt) items at once?

A: The person asking this question may never know a truth: before using the plugin, you should be familiar with the config.yml file. In config.yml, there is an option called sell.max-amount, and I want you to know its purpose by looking at its name.

Q: How to change the max amount limit of buy more menu?

A: There is a option called menu.buy-more.<buy more menu name>.max-amount option in config.yml file, or buy-more-menu.max-amount option in your product configs if you are setting up a separate buy more menu for a certain product.

Q: What does start-apply mean?

A: This means which times this price will apply. If you set it to 5, price will apply after player buy or sell this product 5 times.

This option will only work for ANY or ALL price-mode.

Q: Item dupe when quickly click item outside menu.

A: Some other plugin or mod lead to this problem. Try enable ignore-click-outside option jn config.yml file.

Q: What is different from free version and premium version?

A: Check this page for more info.

Q: Can I set different add lore for each product?

A: Yes, in Shop page we have told you that add-lore also works in each product configs!

Q: Shop menu can not open after use once!

A: Make sure your config.yml is latest format, if not, update it. Or, you are using menu cooldown system, disable it may fix.

Q: How can I translate item name in buy more menu and plugin message?

A: View Localized Item Name page.

Q: Why my item name is in Chinese?

A: Disable Localized Item Name feature.

Q: UltimateShop print Error:XXX message in console.

A: What I want to tell you is already put in the error message itself, like:

Error: Can not get prices section in your shop config!!

If there are no issues with the shop, there is no need to pay attention to it. The error message reported by the plugin is a prompt, and the plugin will automatically attempt to fix it once it detects this error.

Q: How to reset dynamic price?

A: View Dynamic Price page.

> For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ultimateshop.superiormc.cn/llms.txt). Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://ultimateshop.superiormc.cn/info/faq.md).

# ❓FAQ

## Q: Player don't cost money when buy product.

A: That is simply because you give self `*` permission so plugin will bypass price check for you. For common player, it will work correctly.

## Q: My item can not be sold in shop, but I think they are same item.

A: No, actually they have small different, but you dind't find them. The simplest way is to change the `sell-methods` option in `config.yml` from `Bukkit` to `ItemFormat`.

## Q: Does the /shop command has permission?

A: Use `/shop` can directly open a menu called `main`. This is a feature called **Auto Open**, and you can disable it at `config.yml` file with `menu.auto-open.enabled` option. If you only want some players to be exposed to this command, you can set `conditions` for the menu so that only players who meet the specified conditions can open the menu. For more info, please view [Menus](/menu-types/general-menus.md) page.

## Q: Why it say condition not meet when open daily example menu?

A: That menu already has a condition, which you can find in `menus/shop_menu_templates/daily-shop-menu.yml`.

## **Q: Why can I only sell 64x (or other amunt) items at once?**

**A:** The person asking this question may never know a truth: before using the plugin, you should be familiar with the `config.yml` file. In `config.yml`, there is an option called `sell.max-amount`, and I want you to know its purpose by looking at its name.

## Q: How to change the max amount limit of buy more menu?

A: There is a option called `menu.buy-more..max-amount` option in `config.yml` file, or `buy-more-menu.max-amount` option in your product configs if you are setting up a separate buy more menu for a certain product.

## **Q: What does start-apply mean?**

A: This means which times this price will apply. If you set it to 5, price will apply after player buy or sell this product 5 times.

This option will only work for `ANY` or `ALL` price-mode.

## Q: Item dupe when quickly click item outside menu.

A: Some other plugin or mod lead to this problem. Try enable `ignore-click-outside` option jn `config.yml` file.

## Q: What is different from free version and premium version?

A: Check [this](/info/compare.md) page for more info.

## Q: Can I set different add lore for each product?

A: Yes, in [Shop](/shops/shops.md) page we have told you that `add-lore` also works in each product configs!

## Q: Shop menu can not open after use once!

A: Make sure your `config.yml` is latest format, if not, update it. Or, you are using menu cooldown system, disable it may fix.

## Q: How can I translate item name in buy more menu and plugin message?

A: View [Localized Item Name](/features/localized-item-name-premium.md) page.

## Q: Why my item name is in Chinese?

A: Disable [Localized Item Name](/features/localized-item-name-premium.md) feature.

## Q: UltimateShop print Error:XXX message in console.

A: What I want to tell you is already put in the error message itself, like:

#### Error: Can not get prices section in your shop config!!

If there are no issues with the shop, there is no need to pay attention to it. The error message reported by the plugin is a prompt, and the plugin will automatically attempt to fix it once it detects this error.

## Q: How to reset dynamic price?

A: View [Dynamic Price](/dynamic-prices/dynamic-price.md) page.

📦Info

⚙️Install

Install

Put the .jar file into your server's plugins folder.

Stop your server and then restart it. Cannot load plugins in any other way while the server is starting.

When updating plugins, please be sure to remove old versions.

Previously, you used the free version, but now to upgrade to the paid version, you only need to install the paid version on the server and remove the free version. The configuration file of the plugin does not require any changes.

When downgrading from a new game version to an old version on the server where the plugin is located, it is important to remove the items folder from the configuration file.

When using the Localized Item Name feature, it is important to note that when switching server game versions, the previously generated localized files need to be deleted.

UltimateShop is just a shop plugin and does not provide custom economy functionality. If you need a custom economy as your server economy, please find a suitable economy plugin yourself. Vault is not an economy plugin, it is just a dependency plugin for many economy plugins. After installing Vault on the server, it is also necessary to install the economy plugins that support it.

Default configs are just helping you understand the config framework, you need modify them that meet your needs.

> For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ultimateshop.superiormc.cn/llms.txt). Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://ultimateshop.superiormc.cn/info/install.md).

# ⚙️Install

## Install

* Put the `.jar` file into your server's `plugins` folder.
* Stop your server and then restart it. Cannot load plugins in any other way while the server is starting.
* When updating plugins, please be sure to remove old versions.
* Previously, you used the free version, but now to upgrade to the paid version, you only need to install the paid version on the server and remove the free version. The configuration file of the plugin does not require any changes.
* When downgrading from **a new game version** to **an old version** on the server where the plugin is located, it is important to remove the `items` folder from the configuration file.
* When using the [Localized Item Name](/features/localized-item-name-premium.md) feature, it is important to note that when switching server game versions, the previously generated localized files need to be deleted.
* **UltimateShop** is just a shop plugin and does not provide custom economy functionality. If you need a custom economy as your server economy, please find a suitable economy plugin yourself. **Vault** is not an economy plugin, it is just a dependency plugin for many economy plugins. After installing Vault on the server, it is also necessary to install the economy plugins that support it.
* Default configs are just helping you understand the config framework, you need modify them that meet your needs.

📦Info

🚀Performance

UltimateShop is just a shop plugin that usually does not have too much impact on the server. It is usually a performance issue caused by your unreasonable settings or other plugins, such as:

Do not use ANY, ALL price/product mode unless necessary.

Different from CLASSIC_ANY, CLASSIC_ALL mode, ANY and ALL mode, the calculation for each buy or sell is independent. Only use the 2 mode when you set dynamic price or limit.

MMOItems/MythicMobs Item generation performance.

Both plugins are spend much server resource to generate item than vanilla items. If possible and your item is static item with no things like dynamic stat or level requirement, you can try use Save Item instead.

For suggestions below:
The change you need made are all exist in config.yml file.

Disable sell chest.

If you are not using sell chest feature, you can disable this feature to save serve performance.

Copy

sell:
sell-chest:
enabled: false

Set placeholder.click.enabled option to false.

This maybe save server performance.

Copy

click:
# If enabled, {buy-click} and {sell-stick} will display different value according to product status.
# But, it will maybe make server lag if you are running big server and have many products in your shop.
enabled: false

Set cooldown for menu system.

Recommend use when you are running big server, it will make player no longer quickly click and reopen shop menu to make sure UltimateShop not lag your server.

Do not enable auto update GUI feature.

Enabling these options will significantly increase server performance consumption, but buttons within the GUI will be able to automatically update.

In most cases, you just want the GUI to update and display the latest data when we reset buy times or sell times, so you can achieve this idea through use-times.auto-reset-mode option.

If you pursue ultimate plugin performance, it's best not to turn on this option either.

Use BUKKIT item give method.

This item give method has the best performance, but the cost is that there may be some issues with stacking items, and when the player's inventory is full, we can only throw the excess items on the ground instead of preventing the player from further trading.

Use Bukkit sell item match method.

This can save some server performance, but the drawback is that the items to be sold must be identical to the items in the shop, with no differences, even including anvil cost, enchants, etc. (Items with durability and enchantable items basically cannot be sold to the shop because of this)

> For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ultimateshop.superiormc.cn/llms.txt). Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://ultimateshop.superiormc.cn/info/performance.md).

# 🚀Performance

UltimateShop is just a shop plugin that usually does not have too much impact on the server. It is usually a performance issue caused by your unreasonable settings or other plugins, such as:

## Do not use ANY, ALL price/product mode unless necessary.

Different from `CLASSIC_ANY, CLASSIC_ALL` mode, `ANY` and `ALL` mode, the calculation for each buy or sell is independent. Only use the 2 mode when you set dynamic price or limit.

## MMOItems/MythicMobs Item generation performance.

Both plugins are spend much server resource to generate item than vanilla items. If possible and your item is static item with no things like dynamic stat or level requirement, you can try use [Save Item](/features/saved-item-item-manager.md) instead.

{% hint style="info" %}
For suggestions **below**:\
The change you need made are all exist in `config.yml` file.
{% endhint %}

## Disable sell chest.

If you are not using sell chest feature, you can disable this feature to save serve performance.

```yaml
sell:
sell-chest:
enabled: false
```

## Set placeholder.click.enabled option to false.

This maybe save server performance.

```yaml
click:
# If enabled, {buy-click} and {sell-stick} will display different value according to product status.
# But, it will maybe make server lag if you are running big server and have many products in your shop.
enabled: false
```

## Set cooldown for menu system.

Recommend use when you are running big server, it will make player no longer quickly click and reopen shop menu to make sure UltimateShop not lag your server.

```yaml
# Recommend use when you are running big server, it will make player no longer quickly click
# and reopen shop menu to make sure UltimateShop not lag your server.
# In ticks.
cooldown:
click: 6 # Default value is -1, set value greater than 5 is recommended.
reopen: 20 # Default value is -1, set value greater than 5 is recommended.
```

## Do not enable auto update GUI feature.

Enabling these options will significantly increase server performance consumption, but buttons within the GUI will be able to automatically update.

```yaml
menu-update:
# Whether menu will refresh every buttons every 1 second.
# This will refresh placeholder that displayed in display item lore.
# But maybe lead to server lag if you have much online players, and they are all opening shop GUI.
circle-update: false
# Whether menu will refresh every buttons when click any of them.
# This will refresh placeholder that displayed in display item lore.
# But maybe lead to server lag if you have much online players, and they are all opening shop GUI.
click-update: false
# PREMIUM version only, if enabled, can update dynamic value used in GUI title.
title-update:
# Whether gui title will refresh every buttons every 1 second.
# This will refresh placeholder that displayed in menu title.
circle-update: false
# Whether gui title will refresh every buttons when click any of them.
# This will refresh placeholder that displayed in menu title.
click-update: true
resend-items-pack: false
```

In most cases, you just want the GUI to update and display the latest data when we reset buy times or sell times, so you can achieve this idea through `use-times.auto-reset-mode` option.

```yaml
auto-reset-mode: true
```

If you pursue ultimate plugin performance, it's best not to turn on this option either.

```yaml
auto-reset-mode: false
```

## Use BUKKIT item give method.

This item give method has the best performance, but the cost is that there may be some issues with stacking items, and when the player's inventory is full, we can only throw the excess items on the ground instead of preventing the player from further trading.

```yaml
give-item:
# Support value: BUKKIT, SMART
# SMART will cost more server performance but will follow the vanilla max stack to give player item, also support check full.
give-method: BUKKIT
# Only support SMART give method.
check-full: false
```

## Use Bukkit sell item match method.

This can save some server performance, but the drawback is that the items to be sold must be identical to the items in the shop, with no differences, even including anvil cost, enchants, etc. (Items with durability and enchantable items basically cannot be sold to the shop because of this)

```yaml
sell:
# Support Value: Bukkit or ItemFormat.
# For each product, you can add match-item section to make custom sell match method, for more info, please view Wiki.
sell-method: Bukkit
```

🧭Menu Types

🔽Buy More Menus

Buy More selects the number of trade units for an already selected product. One trade unit can contain several items according to the product's configured reward amount. It is not a standalone shop and cannot be opened meaningfully with /shop menu.

Files live in plugins/UltimateShop/menus/buy_more_menus/. The bundled files are buy-more.yml, buy-more-buy.yml and buy-more-sell.yml.

Enable and select the quantity menu

Global settings in config.yml:

Copy

menu:
buy-more-menu:
not-open-when-invalid: true
display-item-max-stack: true
default:
menu: buy-more
max-amount: 693
only-buy:
menu: buy-more-buy
max-amount: 693
only-sell:
menu: buy-more-sell
max-amount: 693

Key under menu.buy-more-menu

Meaning

default.menu, default.max-amount

Menu and maximum trade count when both price directions exist

only-buy.menu, only-buy.max-amount

Defaults for a product without sell prices

only-sell.menu, only-sell.max-amount

Defaults for a product without buy prices

not-open-when-invalid

Block opening a menu whose confirmation buttons are all invalid for that product

display-item-max-stack

Allow preview stacks to use the extended display maximum instead of the material stack limit on supported runtimes

Shop settings.buy-more supplies the shop default. Product buy-more overrides whether that product allows quantity selection. Product buy-more-menu overrides the selected menu and maximum:

Bind the select-amount product operation under menu.click-event (default SHIFT_RIGHT) or use the buy_more_menu action with the required shop/product context. NEVER disables the corresponding click binding. The buy_more_menu action supports shop and item.

Custom Buy More action settings - Premium

The buy_more_menu action also accepts a buy-more-menu section with menu and max-amount for that opening. Custom click actions can select separate buy-only and sell-only menus; see Custom Click Event - Premium.

Inventory amount-selection example

0 is empty unless defined under ordinary buttons. Confirmation and amount IDs must occur in layout. Do not reuse an ID for unrelated control types.

Amount/preview/confirmation keys

All Common menu settings also apply, including title, layout, ordinary buttons, conditions/actions and UI selection.

Additional key

Meaning

amount-items.<id>.display-item

Appearance of an amount control

amount-items.<id>.add-amount

Add a positive/negative amount to the current count

amount-items.<id>.set-amount

Set a fixed count when add-amount is absent or zero; set at least 1

display-items

Ordered list of preview layout IDs; takes precedence over singular display-item

display-item

A single preview marker alternative to display-items

display-items-padding-item

Display Item Format for unused preview slots after the first

display-items-ui.ui

Optional graphical placement/style of a preview; this does not turn Buy More into an ArcMenu screen

confirm-items.<id>.display-item

Confirmation button appearance; {amount} is the selected quantity

confirm-items.<id>.click-action

Optional fixed operation such as buy, sell, buy-or-sell, sell-all; omitted means use the current click operation

confirm-items.<id>.modify-lore

Default true; generate the product price/stock/action lore using the selected amount

amount-items.<id>.menu-visibility, confirm-items.<id>.menu-visibility

Filter a control by presentation

amount-items.<id>.ui, confirm-items.<id>.ui

Graphical placement/style metadata; does not make ArcMenu render an Inventory Buy More menu

Preview stacks split the selected count across preview slots in list order, using the effective stack maximum (99 when enabled, otherwise the material maximum). Extra preview space shows the padding item or air. Preview capacity is visual; it does not replace max-amount. Quantity controls clamp the count to the permitted range. Supply at least one valid confirmation button for the trade direction you intend to support.

Quantity controls by presentation

Presentation

Quantity UI

Inventory

Uses amount-items, preview markers and confirm-items from this file

Bedrock Form

Text input, then product information; no Inventory amount buttons

Native Dialog / Ore

Native amount input, then product information; no Inventory slot layout

ArcMenu

select-amount opens product details directly; plus/minus and scrolling adjust the amount

ArcMenu details require Buy More and a menu, and adjustment requires an available select-amount binding. The same product maximum limits it, but it does not read this file's amount/confirmation layout. Right-click defaults to select-amount and can be changed in ui.renderers.arcmenu.right-click-action.

Without a manual quantity selection, product operations keep default-buy-amount and default-sell-amount independently. After selection, both directions use the chosen count. {buy-amount} and {sell-amount} in generated lore reflect that distinction. Explicit display-item stack amounts are separate from the number of trade units. See Default Trade Amounts.

Form and Dialog labels are configured in their native bedrock and dialog sections; graphical product styling/actions are documented in Graphical UI Layout - Premium. Editing an Inventory confirmation label will not rename a Form information action.

Menu Configuration · UI Modes · Shop Menus

Custom Buy More action settings - Premium

Inventory amount-selection example

Amount/preview/confirmation keys

Quantity controls by presentation

Related documentation

items:

buy-more: true
buy-more-menu:
menu: buy-more
max-amount: 128
# Product, prices and display follow here.

Copy

title: 'Choose amount'
size: 27

- '000000000'
- '01a2b3c00'
- '000D0E000'

material: RED_WOOL
name: '&c-1'

material: GREEN_WOOL

add-amount: 1
3:
display-item:
material: PAPER
name: '&eSet to 64'
set-amount: 64
display-items: [a, b, c]
display-items-padding-item:
material: GRAY_STAINED_GLASS_PANE
name: ' '
confirm-items:
D:
display-item:
material: EMERALD
name: '&aBuy x{amount}'

# Buy More Menus

Buy More selects the number of trade units for an already selected product. One trade unit can contain several items according to the product's configured reward amount. It is not a standalone shop and cannot be opened meaningfully with `/shop menu`.

Files live in `plugins/UltimateShop/menus/buy_more_menus/`. The bundled files are `buy-more.yml`, `buy-more-buy.yml` and `buy-more-sell.yml`.

## Enable and select the quantity menu

Global settings in `config.yml`:

```yaml
menu:
buy-more-menu:
not-open-when-invalid: true
display-item-max-stack: true
default:
menu: buy-more
max-amount: 693
only-buy:
menu: buy-more-buy
max-amount: 693
only-sell:
menu: buy-more-sell
max-amount: 693
```

| Key under `menu.buy-more-menu` | Meaning |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `default.menu`, `default.max-amount` | Menu and maximum trade count when both price directions exist |
| `only-buy.menu`, `only-buy.max-amount` | Defaults for a product without sell prices |
| `only-sell.menu`, `only-sell.max-amount` | Defaults for a product without buy prices |
| `not-open-when-invalid` | Block opening a menu whose confirmation buttons are all invalid for that product |
| `display-item-max-stack` | Allow preview stacks to use the extended display maximum instead of the material stack limit on supported runtimes |

Shop `settings.buy-more` supplies the shop default. Product `buy-more` overrides whether that product allows quantity selection. Product `buy-more-menu` overrides the selected menu and maximum:

```yaml
items:
A:
buy-more: true
buy-more-menu:
menu: buy-more
max-amount: 128
# Product, prices and display follow here.
```

Bind the `select-amount` product operation under `menu.click-event` (default `SHIFT_RIGHT`) or use the [buy\_more\_menu action](/format/action-format.md) with the required shop/product context. `NEVER` disables the corresponding click binding. The `buy_more_menu` action supports `shop` and `item`.

### Custom Buy More action settings - Premium

The `buy_more_menu` action also accepts a `buy-more-menu` section with `menu` and `max-amount` for that opening. Custom click actions can select separate buy-only and sell-only menus; see [Custom Click Event - Premium](/features/custom-click-event-premium.md#example-only-buy-more-menu).

## Inventory amount-selection example

```yaml
title: 'Choose amount'
size: 27
layout:
- '000000000'
- '01a2b3c00'
- '000D0E000'
amount-items:
1:
display-item:
material: RED_WOOL
name: '&c-1'
add-amount: -1
2:
display-item:
material: GREEN_WOOL
name: '&a+1'
add-amount: 1
3:
display-item:
material: PAPER
name: '&eSet to 64'
set-amount: 64
display-items: [a, b, c]
display-items-padding-item:
material: GRAY_STAINED_GLASS_PANE
name: ' '
confirm-items:
D:
display-item:
material: EMERALD
name: '&aBuy x{amount}'
click-action: buy
modify-lore: true
E:
display-item:
material: GOLD_INGOT
name: '&eSell x{amount}'
click-action: sell
modify-lore: true
```

`0` is empty unless defined under ordinary `buttons`. Confirmation and amount IDs must occur in `layout`. Do not reuse an ID for unrelated control types.

## Amount/preview/confirmation keys

All [Common menu settings](/menu-types/general-menus.md) also apply, including title, layout, ordinary buttons, conditions/actions and UI selection.

| Additional key | Meaning |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `amount-items..display-item` | Appearance of an amount control |
| `amount-items..add-amount` | Add a positive/negative amount to the current count |
| `amount-items..set-amount` | Set a fixed count when `add-amount` is absent or zero; set at least 1 |
| `display-items` | Ordered list of preview layout IDs; takes precedence over singular `display-item` |
| `display-item` | A single preview marker alternative to `display-items` |
| `display-items-padding-item` | Display Item Format for unused preview slots after the first |
| `display-items-ui.ui` | Optional graphical placement/style of a preview; this does not turn Buy More into an ArcMenu screen |
| `confirm-items..display-item` | Confirmation button appearance; `{amount}` is the selected quantity |
| `confirm-items..click-action` | Optional fixed operation such as `buy`, `sell`, `buy-or-sell`, `sell-all`; omitted means use the current click operation |
| `confirm-items..modify-lore` | Default true; generate the product price/stock/action lore using the selected amount |
| `amount-items..menu-visibility`, `confirm-items..menu-visibility` | Filter a control by presentation |
| `amount-items..ui`, `confirm-items..ui` | Graphical placement/style metadata; does not make ArcMenu render an Inventory Buy More menu |

Preview stacks split the selected count across preview slots in list order, using the effective stack maximum (99 when enabled, otherwise the material maximum). Extra preview space shows the padding item or air. Preview capacity is visual; it does not replace `max-amount`. Quantity controls clamp the count to the permitted range. Supply at least one valid confirmation button for the trade direction you intend to support.

## Quantity controls by presentation

| Presentation | Quantity UI |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Inventory | Uses `amount-items`, preview markers and `confirm-items` from this file |
| Bedrock Form | Text input, then product information; no Inventory amount buttons |
| Native Dialog / Ore | Native amount input, then product information; no Inventory slot layout |
| ArcMenu | `select-amount` opens product details directly; plus/minus and scrolling adjust the amount |

ArcMenu details require Buy More and a menu, and adjustment requires an available `select-amount` binding. The same product maximum limits it, but it does not read this file's amount/confirmation layout. Right-click defaults to `select-amount` and can be changed in `ui.renderers.arcmenu.right-click-action`.

Without a manual quantity selection, product operations keep `default-buy-amount` and `default-sell-amount` independently. After selection, both directions use the chosen count. `{buy-amount}` and `{sell-amount}` in generated lore reflect that distinction. Explicit display-item stack amounts are separate from the number of trade units. See [Default Trade Amounts](/shops/products.md#default-trade-amounts).

Form and Dialog labels are configured in their native `bedrock` and `dialog` sections; graphical product styling/actions are documented in [Graphical UI Layout - Premium](/menus-getting-started/ui-layout.md). Editing an Inventory confirmation label will not rename a Form information action.

🧭Menu Types

❤️Favourite Menus - Premium

Favourite menus store a player's chosen shop products and their order. Files live in plugins/UltimateShop/menus/favourite_menus/; the bundled example is favourite.yml. Open with /shop menu favourite or an open_menu action. Saved lists are associated with the favourite menu ID, so use that same ID when adding a product.

Files in the dedicated folder are automatically Favourite menus. Common-folder files can use menu-type: favourite (alias favorite) or be listed under menu.favourite-gui.menu in config.yml. Dedicated files do not require that legacy list. Keep IDs unique.

Add products to favourites

The built-in default binds add-favourite to SWAP_OFFHAND (F). Its configured action in menu.click-event-actions.add-favourite uses the add_favourite action:

Copy

type: add_favourite
menu: favourite
shop: '{shop}'
item: '{item}'

Use it within an action list with the relevant shop/product context. Products must allow favourites. Shared Form/Dialog/graphical extra actions can expose the same operation; adding an action label alone does not create its click binding. See Custom Click Event - Premium.

Create a Favourite menu

Copy

title: 'Favourites'
content: 'Your saved products.'
size: 27
layout:
- '000000000'
- '011111110'
- '0000D0000'
result-item: '1'
edit-mode-item:
D:
normal-display-item:
material: NAME_TAG
name: '&eEdit favourites'
editing-display-item:
material: WRITABLE_BOOK
name: '&aFinish editing'
empty-item:
display-item:
material: GRAY_STAINED_GLASS_PANE
name: '&7Empty favourite slot'
result-lore:
- '&7Shop: {shop}'
- '&7Product: {product}'
editing-result-lore:
- '&eLeft: move forward'
- '&eRight: move backward'
- '&cDrop: remove'

Favourite-only keys

All Common menu settings remain available. Ordinary navigation controls belong under buttons.

Additional key

Meaning

result-item

Result marker used in layout

result-items

List of additional result markers; combined with singular result-item; when neither is supplied, marker 6 is used

edit-mode-item.<id>.normal-display-item

Display Item Format when editing is off

edit-mode-item.<id>.editing-display-item

Display when editing is on

edit-mode-item.<id>.display-item

Fallback display if the current normal/editing variant is missing

edit-mode-item.<id>.slot

Optional zero-based fallback slot when the ID is not found in layout

edit-mode-item.<id>.menu-visibility

Show/hide the editing toggle per presentation

edit-mode-item.<id>.ui

Ore/ArcMenu graphical placement and appearance of the toggle

empty-item.display-item

Placeholder shown in unoccupied result slots

empty-item.menu-visibility

Presentation visibility for empty-slot placeholders

empty-item.ui

Graphical placement of empty-slot placeholders

result-lore

Extra lore in normal mode; supports {shop} and {product}

editing-result-lore

Extra lore in edit mode; keep instructions appropriate to the presentation

Edit-toggle displays support {editing} and {edit-mode} (true/false), plus {favourite-amount} and {favorite-amount}. Empty-slot displays support those amount aliases and {slot-index} (one-based result position).

Result slots are filled in saved order, limited by the number of configured result slots. Increasing graphical pagination capacity does not by itself increase that source limit. Use one edit toggle: the runtime keeps one resolved edit-mode button/slot rather than a collection of independent toggles.

Normal and editing modes

In Inventory normal mode, product clicks use the product's configured click operations. Selecting the edit toggle switches to editing; it does not buy or sell. In Inventory editing:

Input

Operation

Left click

Move the product one position forward

Right click

Move it one position backward

Drop / Control-Drop

Remove it from this favourite list

Removing a favourite does not remove shop stock or player items. Toggle editing off to return to product operations. Saved product references and order are shared across presentations.

Presentation-specific behavior

Select presentations with the global/menu dialog.enabled, bedrock.enabled and arcmenu.enabled switches. The ui section only configures Ore/ArcMenu graphical layout.

Presentation

Normal mode

Editing mode

Inventory

Product click bindings

Left/right/drop controls above

Form

Product information Form

Selecting a product opens Forward/Backward/Remove/Back; closing returns to the editing list

Native Dialog / Ore

Product information/actions

Dedicated editing controls; native Dialog omits empty result slots

ArcMenu

Product cards and shared actions/details

Forward/Backward/Remove buttons on each card; also left/right/middle edit clicks (middle removes)

Form can display configured empty-slot buttons. Ore/ArcMenu require graphical ui.placement for the toggle and ordinary controls, and ui.products.placement for result cards. The bundled example disables graphical placement on empty slots.

Global Form editing text is under menu.bedrock.favourite-edit: title, content, and buttons.forward, backward, remove, back. Dialog has the same structure under menu.dialog.favourite-edit. Titles/content accept {item-name}.

ArcMenu card labels default to the Form favourite edit labels. Override them per menu with ui.text.favourite-edit.forward, backward, remove. Use presentation conditions in result lore when different clients need different instructions; see Add Lore.

# Favourite Menus - Premium

Favourite menus store a player's chosen shop products and their order. Files live in `plugins/UltimateShop/menus/favourite_menus/`; the bundled example is `favourite.yml`. Open with `/shop menu favourite` or an `open_menu` action. Saved lists are associated with the favourite menu ID, so use that same ID when adding a product.

Files in the dedicated folder are automatically Favourite menus. Common-folder files can use `menu-type: favourite` (alias `favorite`) or be listed under `menu.favourite-gui.menu` in `config.yml`. Dedicated files do not require that legacy list. Keep IDs unique.

## Add products to favourites

The built-in default binds `add-favourite` to `SWAP_OFFHAND` (F). Its configured action in `menu.click-event-actions.add-favourite` uses the `add_favourite` action:

```yaml
type: add_favourite
menu: favourite
shop: '{shop}'
item: '{item}'
```

Use it within an action list with the relevant shop/product context. Products must allow favourites. Shared Form/Dialog/graphical extra actions can expose the same operation; adding an action label alone does not create its click binding. See [Custom Click Event - Premium](/features/custom-click-event-premium.md).

## Create a Favourite menu

```yaml
title: 'Favourites'
content: 'Your saved products.'
size: 27
layout:
- '000000000'
- '011111110'
- '0000D0000'
result-item: '1'
edit-mode-item:
D:
normal-display-item:
material: NAME_TAG
name: '&eEdit favourites'
editing-display-item:
material: WRITABLE_BOOK
name: '&aFinish editing'
empty-item:
display-item:
material: GRAY_STAINED_GLASS_PANE
name: '&7Empty favourite slot'
result-lore:
- '&7Shop: {shop}'
- '&7Product: {product}'
editing-result-lore:
- '&eLeft: move forward'
- '&eRight: move backward'
- '&cDrop: remove'
```

## Favourite-only keys

All [Common menu settings](/menu-types/general-menus.md) remain available. Ordinary navigation controls belong under `buttons`.

| Additional key | Meaning |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `result-item` | Result marker used in `layout` |
| `result-items` | List of additional result markers; combined with singular `result-item`; when neither is supplied, marker `6` is used |
| `edit-mode-item..normal-display-item` | Display Item Format when editing is off |
| `edit-mode-item..editing-display-item` | Display when editing is on |
| `edit-mode-item..display-item` | Fallback display if the current normal/editing variant is missing |
| `edit-mode-item..slot` | Optional zero-based fallback slot when the ID is not found in `layout` |
| `edit-mode-item..menu-visibility` | Show/hide the editing toggle per presentation |
| `edit-mode-item..ui` | Ore/ArcMenu graphical placement and appearance of the toggle |
| `empty-item.display-item` | Placeholder shown in unoccupied result slots |
| `empty-item.menu-visibility` | Presentation visibility for empty-slot placeholders |
| `empty-item.ui` | Graphical placement of empty-slot placeholders |
| `result-lore` | Extra lore in normal mode; supports `{shop}` and `{product}` |
| `editing-result-lore` | Extra lore in edit mode; keep instructions appropriate to the presentation |

Edit-toggle displays support `{editing}` and `{edit-mode}` (true/false), plus `{favourite-amount}` and `{favorite-amount}`. Empty-slot displays support those amount aliases and `{slot-index}` (one-based result position).

Result slots are filled in saved order, limited by the number of configured result slots. Increasing graphical pagination capacity does not by itself increase that source limit. Use one edit toggle: the runtime keeps one resolved edit-mode button/slot rather than a collection of independent toggles.

## Normal and editing modes

In Inventory normal mode, product clicks use the product's configured click operations. Selecting the edit toggle switches to editing; it does not buy or sell. In Inventory editing:

| Input | Operation |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| Left click | Move the product one position forward |
| Right click | Move it one position backward |
| Drop / Control-Drop | Remove it from this favourite list |

Removing a favourite does not remove shop stock or player items. Toggle editing off to return to product operations. Saved product references and order are shared across presentations.

## Presentation-specific behavior

Select presentations with the global/menu `dialog.enabled`, `bedrock.enabled` and `arcmenu.enabled` switches. The `ui` section only configures Ore/ArcMenu graphical layout.

| Presentation | Normal mode | Editing mode |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Inventory | Product click bindings | Left/right/drop controls above |
| Form | Product information Form | Selecting a product opens Forward/Backward/Remove/Back; closing returns to the editing list |
| Native Dialog / Ore | Product information/actions | Dedicated editing controls; native Dialog omits empty result slots |
| ArcMenu | Product cards and shared actions/details | Forward/Backward/Remove buttons on each card; also left/right/middle edit clicks (middle removes) |

Form can display configured empty-slot buttons. Ore/ArcMenu require graphical `ui.placement` for the toggle and ordinary controls, and `ui.products.placement` for result cards. The bundled example disables graphical placement on empty slots.

Global Form editing text is under `menu.bedrock.favourite-edit`: `title`, `content`, and `buttons.forward`, `backward`, `remove`, `back`. Dialog has the same structure under `menu.dialog.favourite-edit`. Titles/content accept `{item-name}`.

ArcMenu card labels default to the Form favourite edit labels. Override them per menu with `ui.text.favourite-edit.forward`, `backward`, `remove`. Use presentation conditions in result lore when different clients need different instructions; see [Add Lore](/advanced-menus-and-support/display-item-add-lore.md).

🧭Menu Types

🔲Common Menus

A Common menu is a navigation/action screen. It displays buttons you define; it does not automatically load a shop's products.

Create one

Save as plugins/UltimateShop/menus/common_menus/main.yml:

Copy

title: '&8Main Menu'
size: 9
layout:
- '000A0X000'
buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: WHEAT
name: '&aFarming'
actions:
1:
type: shop_menu
shop: farming
X:
display-item:
material: BARRIER
name: '&cClose'
actions:
1:
type: close

A is placed at the fourth slot and X at the sixth. The farming shop must exist; alternatively use type: open_menu and menu: <menu-id> to open another Common menu. Reload with /shop reload, then use /shop menu main.

Common menu keys

Key

Purpose

title

Screen title

size, layout

Inventory capacity and slot markers

buttons

Actions and display item for each marker

conditions

Conditions required to open the whole menu

open-actions, close-actions

Menu lifecycle actions

dynamic-layout

Conditional/ordered layout alternatives where supported

dialog, bedrock, arcmenu

Client-specific presentation switches and content

ui

Ore/ArcMenu graphical drawing and entry positioning

Keep conditions for menu entry separate from buttons.A.conditions for individual click actions.

Custom menu command - Premium

Use custom-command.name and custom-command.description to register a command for this menu.

Dynamic layout - Premium

Use dynamic-layout for player-dependent layout markers and ordered alternatives. See Conditional Display - Premium.

Use another presentation - Premium

For a native Dialog, add to the menu root:

Also enable menu.dialog.enabled in config.yml. To use graphical Ore, set dialog.layout: ore and configure ui.layout and buttons.<id>.ui.placement. To use ArcMenu, enable global and menu arcmenu.enabled, install its integration and set graphical placements. For Bedrock Form, use menu bedrock.enabled/content and global menu.bedrock.enabled.

Learn presentation priority in 🎨 UI modes and graphical coordinates in 📐 Layout - Premium.

Alternative Common-folder menu types

The dedicated search_menus, favourite_menus and item_sell_menus folders choose those menu types automatically. Files placed in common_menus can also opt in with root menu-type: search, favourite / favorite, or item-sell / item_sell. Search/Favourite classification may also follow the global menu lists. Prefer the dedicated folder for a new menu, and do not reuse an ID across types.

Troubleshooting

If a button is missing, verify layout contains its ID, that buttons.<id> exists, that conditions pass and that menu-visibility allows the active presentation. For Ore/ArcMenu, ensure the button has a graphical ui.placement; inventory coordinates do not create graphical positions.

# Common Menus

A Common menu is a navigation/action screen. It displays **buttons you define**; it does not automatically load a shop's products.

## Create one

Save as `plugins/UltimateShop/menus/common_menus/main.yml`:

```yaml
title: '&8Main Menu'
size: 9
layout:
- '000A0X000'
buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: WHEAT
name: '&aFarming'
actions:
1:
type: shop_menu
shop: farming
X:
display-item:
material: BARRIER
name: '&cClose'
actions:
1:
type: close
```

`A` is placed at the fourth slot and `X` at the sixth. The `farming` shop must exist; alternatively use `type: open_menu` and `menu: ` to open another Common menu. Reload with `/shop reload`, then use `/shop menu main`.

## Common menu keys

| Key | Purpose |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `title` | Screen title |
| `size`, `layout` | Inventory capacity and slot markers |
| `buttons` | Actions and display item for each marker |
| `conditions` | Conditions required to open the whole menu |
| `open-actions`, `close-actions` | Menu lifecycle actions |
| `dynamic-layout` | Conditional/ordered layout alternatives where supported |
| `dialog`, `bedrock`, `arcmenu` | Client-specific presentation switches and content |
| `ui` | Ore/ArcMenu graphical drawing and entry positioning |

Keep `conditions` for menu entry separate from `buttons.A.conditions` for individual click actions.

## Custom menu command - Premium

Use `custom-command.name` and `custom-command.description` to register a command for this menu.

## Dynamic layout - Premium

Use `dynamic-layout` for player-dependent layout markers and ordered alternatives. See [Conditional Display - Premium](/advanced-menus-and-support/conditional-display-premium.md).

## Use another presentation - Premium

For a native Dialog, add to the **menu root**:

```yaml
dialog:
enabled: true
layout: multi-action
content: '&7Choose a category'
button-width: 150
columns: 2
```

Also enable `menu.dialog.enabled` in `config.yml`. To use graphical Ore, set `dialog.layout: ore` **and** configure `ui.layout` and `buttons..ui.placement`. To use ArcMenu, enable global and menu `arcmenu.enabled`, install its integration and set graphical placements. For Bedrock Form, use menu `bedrock.enabled/content` and global `menu.bedrock.enabled`.

Learn presentation priority in [🎨 UI modes](/menu-ui-modes/ui-overview.md) and graphical coordinates in [📐 Layout - Premium](/menus-getting-started/ui-layout.md).

## Alternative Common-folder menu types

The dedicated `search_menus`, `favourite_menus` and `item_sell_menus` folders choose those menu types automatically. Files placed in `common_menus` can also opt in with root `menu-type: search`, `favourite` / `favorite`, or `item-sell` / `item_sell`. Search/Favourite classification may also follow the global menu lists. Prefer the dedicated folder for a new menu, and do not reuse an ID across types.

## Troubleshooting

If a button is missing, verify `layout` contains its ID, that `buttons.` exists, that conditions pass and that `menu-visibility` allows the active presentation. For Ore/ArcMenu, ensure the button has a graphical `ui.placement`; inventory coordinates do not create graphical positions.

[🧱 Buttons and slot markers](/menus-getting-started/layout-and-buttons.md) · [🛍️ Shop menus](/menu-types/shop-menus.md) · [🩺 Troubleshooting](/advanced-menus-and-support/troubleshooting.md).

Copy

title: 'Sell Items'
size: 54
max-sell-amount: -1

- '0IIIIIII0'
- '0IIIIIII0'
- '000000000'
- '0000C0X00'

material: EMERALD

- '&7Original price: &f{original-price}'
- '&7Final multiplier: &fx{multiplier}'

- '&7Unsellable items: &f{unsellable-amount}'

Item Sell-specific keys

Common title, size, layout, buttons, open conditions and open/close actions are described in Common menus.

Additional key

Meaning

input-item

Input layout marker, default I

input-items

Additional input markers, combined with input-item

confirm-item

Confirmation layout marker, default C; may occur in multiple slots

confirm-button.display-item

Display Item Format for the confirmation control

max-sell-amount

Maximum product trade units sold across all input slots per confirmation; -1 means unlimited

Only input slots accept the items to be sold. Use the layout token rules for longer IDs. The confirmation appearance is configured in confirm-button, not as a Buy More confirm-items entry. This menu's confirmation has a built-in sale handler; its name/lore does not define the sale formula.

The preview placeholders are:

Placeholder

Value

{price}

Final reward after global sell multiplier and applicable item-aware modifiers

{original-price}

Reward before those multipliers

{multiplier}

Combined effective sell multiplier

{item-amount}

Amount currently eligible to sell

{unsellable-amount}

Amount currently not eligible to sell

Preview is recalculated from input. Confirmation still runs normal product sell validation, including conditions, player/server limits, actions, events and logging. Unsupported or unsold items remain in the menu and return on close. Display/confirmation icons are not part of the player's sale stock.

Products with price-modifier: true must be sold through Item Sell so the calculation can inspect the supplied item. The menu has no independent modifier formula; configure modifiers on the product. Select the routing target globally:

Form/Dialog shop listings first open product information so buying and selling remain separate choices; choosing the routed sell operation opens the physical Inventory menu.

This is an Inventory deposit interface, including for players whose ordinary shops use Form, Dialog, Ore or ArcMenu. Its bundled ui settings do not create Form input slots or ArcMenu drag/drop sale controls. Configure Inventory size, layout, input and confirmation markers for this screen.

max-sell-amount belongs to this menu and caps the combined confirmation. The global sell engine still applies its own restrictions; raising this value does not bypass stock, limits or product conditions. See Price Modifier for calculation and Sell Multiplier - Premium for reward multipliers.

# Item Sell Menus

Item Sell lets players place real item stacks into input slots, preview their adjusted sell value, and explicitly confirm the sale. Closing without confirming returns the items. This differs from [Sell All](/menu-types/sell-all-menu.md), which sells on close.

Files live in `plugins/UltimateShop/menus/item_sell_menus/`; the bundled example is `item-sell.yml`. Open with `/shop menu item-sell` or an `open_menu` action. The dedicated folder determines the type; files in `common_menus` can use `menu-type: item-sell` (alias `item_sell`).

## Inventory deposit example

```yaml
title: 'Sell Items'
size: 54
max-sell-amount: -1
layout:
- '000000000'
- '0IIIIIII0'
- '0IIIIIII0'
- '0IIIIIII0'
- '000000000'
- '0000C0X00'
input-item: 'I'
confirm-item: 'C'
confirm-button:
display-item:
material: EMERALD
name: '&aConfirm Sale'
lore:
- '&7Price: &f{price}'
- '&7Original price: &f{original-price}'
- '&7Final multiplier: &fx{multiplier}'
- '&7Sellable items: &f{item-amount}'
- '&7Unsellable items: &f{unsellable-amount}'
buttons:
X:
display-item:
material: BARRIER
name: '&cClose'
actions:
1:
type: close
```

Undefined `0` slots are empty but are not input slots; define filler button `0` if desired. The example intentionally includes only a confirm control and a Close button.

## Item Sell-specific keys

Common title, size, layout, buttons, open conditions and open/close actions are described in [Common menus](/menu-types/general-menus.md).

| Additional key | Meaning |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `input-item` | Input layout marker, default `I` |
| `input-items` | Additional input markers, combined with `input-item` |
| `confirm-item` | Confirmation layout marker, default `C`; may occur in multiple slots |
| `confirm-button.display-item` | Display Item Format for the confirmation control |
| `max-sell-amount` | Maximum product trade units sold across all input slots per confirmation; `-1` means unlimited |

Only input slots accept the items to be sold. Use the layout token rules for longer IDs. The confirmation appearance is configured in `confirm-button`, not as a Buy More `confirm-items` entry. This menu's confirmation has a built-in sale handler; its name/lore does not define the sale formula.

The preview placeholders are:

| Placeholder | Value |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `{price}` | Final reward after global sell multiplier and applicable item-aware modifiers |
| `{original-price}` | Reward before those multipliers |
| `{multiplier}` | Combined effective sell multiplier |
| `{item-amount}` | Amount currently eligible to sell |
| `{unsellable-amount}` | Amount currently not eligible to sell |

Preview is recalculated from input. Confirmation still runs normal product sell validation, including conditions, player/server limits, actions, events and logging. Unsupported or unsold items remain in the menu and return on close. Display/confirmation icons are not part of the player's sale stock.

## Item-aware price modifiers

Products with `price-modifier: true` must be sold through Item Sell so the calculation can inspect the supplied item. The menu has no independent modifier formula; configure modifiers on the product. Select the routing target globally:

```yaml
sell:
price-modifier:
item-sell-menu:
enabled: true
menu: item-sell
```

For those products, `sell` and `sell-all` route to the selected Item Sell menu. Buy, quantity selection and custom operations keep their normal behaviour. Form/Dialog shop listings first open product information so buying and selling remain separate choices; choosing the routed sell operation opens the physical Inventory menu.

## Presentation and related settings

This is an Inventory deposit interface, including for players whose ordinary shops use Form, Dialog, Ore or ArcMenu. Its bundled `ui` settings do not create Form input slots or ArcMenu drag/drop sale controls. Configure Inventory `size`, `layout`, input and confirmation markers for this screen.

`max-sell-amount` belongs to this menu and caps the combined confirmation. The global sell engine still applies its own restrictions; raising this value does not bypass stock, limits or product conditions. See [Price Modifier](/shops/price-modifier.md) for calculation and [Sell Multiplier - Premium](/shops/sell-multiplier-premium.md) for reward multipliers.

## Related documentation

[Inventory UI](/menu-ui-modes/inventory-ui.md) · [Sell All](/menu-types/sell-all-menu.md) · [Troubleshooting](/advanced-menus-and-support/troubleshooting.md)

🔍Search Menus - Premium

Search menus find products visible to the player by physical item and/or name. Store files in plugins/UltimateShop/menus/search_menus/; the bundled example is search.yml. Open with /shop menu search or an open_menu action.

A file in this folder is automatically a Search menu. For a file in menus/common_menus/, use menu-type: search or list its ID under menu.search-gui.menu in config.yml. Dedicated-folder files do not need that list. Keep IDs unique.

Create an Inventory Search menu

Copy

title: 'Search'
content: 'Find a product.'
size: 27
layout:
- '000HNC000'
- '001111100'
- '066666660'
input-item: '1'
result-item: '6'
action-items:
H:
action-type: input-name
display-item:
material: HOPPER
name: '&eEnter a name'
C:
action-type: clear-search
display-item:
material: BARRIER
name: '&cClear'
state-items:
N:
empty-input:
display-item:
material: PAPER
name: '&7Waiting for input'
has-input:
display-item:
material: COMPASS
name: '&a{showing-amount}/{result-amount} results'
no-result-item:
slot: 22
display-item:
material: BARRIER
name: '&cNo results'
result-lore:
- '&7Shop: {shop}'
- '&7Product: {product}'

Search-only keys

The Common menu settings remain available. Use ordinary buttons for Back/Close/navigation.

Additional key

Meaning

input-item

Single input-slot marker, default 1 when no input markers are configured

input-items

Additional input markers; combined with input-item

result-item

Result-slot marker, default 6; occurrences determine how many results can be shown

action-items.<id>.action-type

input-name (alias search-name) for keyword entry; clear-search to clear the search

action-items.<id>.display-item

Appearance of the special action button

clear-search-item.<id>

Legacy action-button section; defaults action-type to clear-search

state-items.<id>.empty-input.display-item

Display before items/keywords are present

state-items.<id>.has-input.display-item

Display when search input is present

no-result-item.slot

Fixed Inventory slot, zero-based; -1 means no valid slot

no-result-item.display-item

Display when a search has no matches

result-lore

Extra lore on result entries; {shop} and {product} identify the source

Special button menu-visibility

Boolean presentation visibility for a special button

Special button ui.placement / ui.appearance

Ore/ArcMenu position and appearance

Layout markers use the normal token rules, including backtick-delimited longer IDs. Do not fill input/result markers with ordinary buttons. Place each special action/state ID in root layout; use a valid no-result-item.slot. Result capacity remains relevant to non-Inventory views.

Status display placeholders are {result-amount} (all matches), {showing-amount} (shown matches), {input-amount} (physical input count) and {name-keyword} (keyword). These are search status values, not global placeholders available in arbitrary menus.

Search and input lifecycle

Inventory input slots accept physical item stacks. Search finds shop products linked to those items; a keyword filters by product/item names. Text-only search works without item stacks. Name matching uses the shared item-name/localization system; see Localized Item Name - Premium.

In Inventory, input-name opens a chat prompt. The shared cancellation and clearing settings in config.yml are:

{lang} uses the configured language value. Cancel leaves the prior keyword; clear removes it. Clear-search also returns physical input items in Inventory. Closing/navigating away returns remaining input rather than consuming display/result icons. Result icons are GUI items, not player-owned stock.

How search differs by presentation

Presentation

Search input and controls

Inventory

Physical item slots, chat keyword entry, action/state/no-result items

Form

Dedicated Search button opens a Custom Form; ordinary buttons are included; no physical input or Inventory special status controls

Native Dialog / Ore

Keyword input and result information; no physical item deposit filter

ArcMenu

Chat keyword entry, clear-search, action/state/no-result controls, graphical result cards

Form opens its home first. Search input prefills the previous keyword; cancel returns to that home and preserves it. Form/Dialog blank keywords show no products. Selecting a result opens information; Back restores the search and keyword. Editing/submitting/cancelling the built-in input flow does not repeatedly run menu open/close actions. Ordinary navigation buttons leave the search flow and run with LEFT click in Form/Dialog.

Form text defaults are menu.bedrock.search.input and menu.bedrock.search.buttons.search; Dialog uses menu.dialog.search.*. Chat keyword controls still use the prompt keywords above. Choose presentations through the global/menu dialog.enabled, bedrock.enabled and arcmenu.enabled switches.

For ArcMenu/Ore, configure ui.layout, ui.products.placement, and ui.placement on graphical controls. Layout pagination does not remove the result-slot capacity defined at root. See ArcMenu - Premium and Dialog - Premium and Ore - Premium for exact renderer differences.

## How search differs by presentation

| Presentation | Search input and controls |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Inventory | Physical item slots, chat keyword entry, action/state/no-result items |
| Form | Dedicated Search button opens a Custom Form; ordinary buttons are included; no physical input or Inventory special status controls |
| Native Dialog / Ore | Keyword input and result information; no physical item deposit filter |
| ArcMenu | Chat keyword entry, clear-search, action/state/no-result controls, graphical result cards |

Form opens its home first. Search input prefills the previous keyword; cancel returns to that home and preserves it. Form/Dialog blank keywords show no products. Selecting a result opens information; Back restores the search and keyword. Editing/submitting/cancelling the built-in input flow does not repeatedly run menu open/close actions. Ordinary navigation buttons leave the search flow and run with LEFT click in Form/Dialog.

Form text defaults are `menu.bedrock.search.input` and `menu.bedrock.search.buttons.search`; Dialog uses `menu.dialog.search.*`. Chat keyword controls still use the prompt keywords above. Choose presentations through the global/menu `dialog.enabled`, `bedrock.enabled` and `arcmenu.enabled` switches.

For ArcMenu/Ore, configure `ui.layout`, `ui.products.placement`, and `ui.placement` on graphical controls. Layout pagination does not remove the result-slot capacity defined at root. See [ArcMenu - Premium](/menu-ui-modes/arcmenu-menus-premium.md) and [Dialog - Premium](/menu-ui-modes/dialog-menus-premium.md) and [Ore - Premium](/menu-ui-modes/ore-menus-premium.md) for exact renderer differences.

## Related documentation

[UI Modes](/menu-ui-modes/ui-overview.md) · [Layout and Buttons](/menus-getting-started/layout-and-buttons.md) · [Troubleshooting](/advanced-menus-and-support/troubleshooting.md)
