# Sell All Menu

Sell All is a single global Inventory interface: players deposit items, then close the window to sell them. It does not use a file in `menus/` and does not have a separate confirmation button. For explicit confirmation and price preview, use [Item Sell](/menu-types/item-sell-menus.md).

## Open Sell All

`/shop sellall` requires `ultimateshop.sellall`. A menu button can use the `sell_all_menu` action:

```yaml
actions:
1:
type: sell_all_menu
```

This remains an Inventory interface even when the source shop/menu uses Form, Dialog, Ore or ArcMenu.

## Global configuration

In `config.yml`:

```yaml
menu:
sell-all:
size: 54
title: '{lang}'
black-slots: []
```

| Key under `menu.sell-all` | Meaning |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `size` | Inventory size: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45 or 54 |
| `title` | Title; `{lang}` uses the matching language override |
| `black-slots` | Zero-based slot numbers that reject item placement, for example `[0, 1, 2]` |

Configure excluded product references under `sell.sell-all.ignore-items` in `config.yml`, using `shop-id;;product-id`. This menu does not support common-menu layout/buttons, `ui.layout`, per-file modes or multiple independent menu IDs.

## Sale behavior

Closing scans shop products visible to the player, skips excluded references and runs the normal sell flow against the deposited inventory. Product conditions, prices, player/server limits and applicable sell multipliers still apply. Global `sell.max-amount` limits the sell engine (fallback 128); it is not this inventory's slot count or an Item Sell `max-sell-amount`.

The sale summary reports amount, reward and effective multiplier. Items that were not sold are returned to the player, or dropped if they cannot fit. Closing an empty menu does not create a reward. Products requiring item-aware price modifiers must use the configured Item Sell flow; Sell All does not replace that requirement.

## Related documentation

[Inventory UI](/menu-ui-modes/inventory-ui.md) · [Item Sell](/menu-types/item-sell-menus.md) · [Troubleshooting](/advanced-menus-and-support/troubleshooting.md)

> For the complete documentation index, see [llms.txt](https://ultimateshop.superiormc.cn/llms.txt). Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://ultimateshop.superiormc.cn/menu-types/shop-menus.md).

# Shop Menus

A shop file defines **products, prices and trading**. A shop-menu template defines **which entries appear and where**, plus navigation buttons. One template may be reused by many shops.

## Two files, two responsibilities

* Shop file: `plugins/UltimateShop/shops/.yml`.
* Template: `plugins/UltimateShop/menus/shop_menu_templates/.yml`.
* `settings.menu` inside the shop selects a template.
* Open with `/shop menu ` or a `shop_menu` action.

## Example 1: menu template

Create `menus/shop_menu_templates/farming.yml`:

```yaml
title: '{shop-name}'
size: 9
layout:
- '0000A0000'
```

`A` identifies a product supplied by the **shop**, not a button defined in the template.

## Example 2: shop file

Create `shops/farming.yml`:

```yaml
settings:
shop-name: '&aFarming'
menu: farming
items:
A:
display-item:
material: WHEAT
name: '&eWheat'
products:
1:
material: WHEAT
buy-prices:
1:
economy-plugin: Vault
amount: 5
```

This example needs your Vault-compatible economy. Reload and open `/shop menu farming`. For supported product/pricing variants, follow [Product configuration](/shops/products.md).

## Override a template for one shop

Use `settings.menu-settings` in the **shop** file:

```yaml
settings:
menu: farming
menu-settings:
title: '&aFarming Specials'
dialog:
enabled: true
layout: multi-action
bedrock:
enabled: true
content: '&7Browse farming products'
```

Overrides are applied to the template *before* global graphical `menu.ui` defaults fill any missing graphical fields. `settings.menu-settings` does **not** belong in `config.yml` or a menu template.

## Adding navigation buttons

A template can define its own buttons:

```yaml
buttons:
X:
display-item:
material: ARROW
name: '&eBack'
actions:
1:
type: back
```

Add `X` to an available `layout` slot. Product IDs and ordinary buttons must not collide in the visible layout. Products can also define `menu-visibility`, `display-conditions` and graphical `ui.placement`.

## Inventory / Dialog / Ore / ArcMenu / Form

The **same shop items** can appear in different presentations. Inventory uses the template's root `layout`. Native Dialog and Form collect items as lists; Ore and ArcMenu use `ui.layout`, `ui.products.placement` and individual button `ui.placement`. A blank graphical area does not automatically create shop-category buttons.

Use [UI selection](/menu-ui-modes/ui-overview.md) and [Graphical layout - Premium](/menus-getting-started/ui-layout.md) for the prerequisites and full configuration.

## If a product is missing

Check that `settings.menu` names a real template, `items.A` exists, `layout` references `A` for Inventory, the product is permitted for the player, and the product's `menu-visibility` and display conditions are satisfied. If graphical settings seem unchanged, check menu/template `ui` and the shop's `settings.menu-settings.ui`; explicit overrides take priority.

[Quantity selection](/menu-types/buy-more-menus.md) · [Search - Premium](/menu-types/search-menus-premium.md) · [Troubleshooting](/advanced-menus-and-support/troubleshooting.md).

🖥️Menu UI Modes

✨ArcMenu UI - Premium

ArcMenu presents Common, Shop, Search and Favourite menus as interactive graphical screens. It shares ui.layout, ui.products, ui.placement and ui.theme with Ore, but uses its own client integration and interaction model.

Enable ArcMenu

In config.yml:

Copy

menu:
arcmenu:
enabled: true

In your menu:

Copy

title: '&8Categories'
size: 9
layout:
- '0000A0000'
arcmenu:
enabled: true
content: '&7Choose a category'
buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: WHEAT
name: '&aFarming'
actions:
1:
type: shop_menu
shop: farming
ui:
appearance: button
placement:
area: sidebar
order: 0

This uses the default global menu.ui.layout.areas.sidebar graphical area. Install a compatible ArcMenu integration and required client resources. If both ArcMenu and Dialog are enabled, Java players use ArcMenu first when available. If ArcMenu cannot open, the menu-opening flow can attempt Dialog/Ore, then Inventory. Bedrock players use their separate bedrock.enabled selection.

Product interaction

Graphical product cards use ui.products.actions.primary for up to two primary operation buttons and ui.products.actions.extra for an extra-action menu.

Listing an action does not create a trade binding. Available actions still come from menu.click-event and product overrides.

select-amount normally opens ArcMenu product details; quantity adjustment requires Buy More to be enabled for the product and a suitable quantity binding.

Product right-click defaults to select-amount. Change it with ui.renderers.arcmenu.right-click-action.

A shop's default buy/sell quantities apply until the player selects another quantity.

ArcMenu product details are not the Inventory Buy More menu. The latter's amount-items and layout do not control ArcMenu's detail panel.

ArcMenu graphical settings

Defaults live at menu.ui.renderers.arcmenu; most renderer settings support per-menu overrides at ui.renderers.arcmenu. update-interval is currently read only from the global menu.ui.renderers.arcmenu.update-interval path.

Key relative to ui.renderers.arcmenu

Effect

right-click-action

Direct action triggered by product right-click

screen-scale

Overall graphical scale

update-interval

Global only: graphical refresh interval, in ticks (minimum 5)

animation.enabled/duration

Opening animation

more-menu.columns

Extra-action popup layout

tooltip.enabled/width/font-size/padding

Hover-tooltip visibility and appearance

The renderer constrains numeric settings to supported ranges. Very large fonts can truncate text; use sensible area and card sizes rather than relying on scale alone.

Layout and theme are shared with Ore

Define a canvas, named areas and optional pagination under menu ui.layout or global menu.ui.layout. Ordinary buttons require ui.placement; products use ui.products.placement unless overridden. In Search/Favourite screens the root result-slot count still limits source results, regardless of how many cards a graphical area could hold.

See 📐 Graphical layout - Premium for the complete schema and correct scopes. ArcMenu does not require Ore's generated pack merely to display its own controls; follow the ArcMenu integration's client setup. The /shop dialogpack command concerns Ore assets.

Troubleshooting

If Inventory opens, check the two ArcMenu switches, plugin integration, resource setup and supported menu type. Item Sell and Sell All require physical inventories; Buy More uses ArcMenu product details instead of a separate Inventory-style ArcMenu screen. Use Menu troubleshooting for symptoms.

🎨 Presentation selection · 📐 Layout - Premium · 🪨 Ore - Premium.

# ArcMenu UI - Premium

ArcMenu presents Common, Shop, Search and Favourite menus as interactive graphical screens. It shares `ui.layout`, `ui.products`, `ui.placement` and `ui.theme` with Ore, but uses its own client integration and interaction model.

## Enable ArcMenu

In `config.yml`:

```yaml
menu:
arcmenu:
enabled: true
```

In your menu:

```yaml
title: '&8Categories'
size: 9
layout:
- '0000A0000'
arcmenu:
enabled: true
content: '&7Choose a category'
buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: WHEAT
name: '&aFarming'
actions:
1:
type: shop_menu
shop: farming
ui:
appearance: button
placement:
area: sidebar
order: 0
```

This uses the default global `menu.ui.layout.areas.sidebar` graphical area. Install a compatible ArcMenu integration and required client resources. If both ArcMenu and Dialog are enabled, Java players use **ArcMenu first** when available. If ArcMenu cannot open, the menu-opening flow can attempt Dialog/Ore, then Inventory. Bedrock players use their separate `bedrock.enabled` selection.

## Product interaction

* Graphical product cards use `ui.products.actions.primary` for up to two primary operation buttons and `ui.products.actions.extra` for an extra-action menu.
* Listing an action does not create a trade binding. Available actions still come from `menu.click-event` and product overrides.
* `select-amount` normally opens ArcMenu product details; quantity adjustment requires Buy More to be enabled for the product and a suitable quantity binding.
* Product right-click defaults to `select-amount`. Change it with `ui.renderers.arcmenu.right-click-action`.
* A shop's default buy/sell quantities apply until the player selects another quantity.

ArcMenu product details are **not** the Inventory Buy More menu. The latter's `amount-items` and `layout` do not control ArcMenu's detail panel.

## ArcMenu graphical settings

Defaults live at `menu.ui.renderers.arcmenu`; most renderer settings support per-menu overrides at `ui.renderers.arcmenu`. **`update-interval` is currently read only from the global `menu.ui.renderers.arcmenu.update-interval` path.**

```yaml
ui:
renderers:
arcmenu:
right-click-action: select-amount
screen-scale: 1.35
update-interval: 20
animation:
enabled: true
duration: 8
more-menu:
columns: 1
tooltip:
enabled: true
width: 260
font-size: 0.9
padding: 8
```

| Key relative to `ui.renderers.arcmenu` | Effect |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `right-click-action` | Direct action triggered by product right-click |
| `screen-scale` | Overall graphical scale |
| `update-interval` | **Global only:** graphical refresh interval, in ticks (minimum 5) |
| `animation.enabled/duration` | Opening animation |
| `more-menu.columns` | Extra-action popup layout |
| `tooltip.enabled/width/font-size/padding` | Hover-tooltip visibility and appearance |

The renderer constrains numeric settings to supported ranges. Very large fonts can truncate text; use sensible area and card sizes rather than relying on scale alone.

## Layout and theme are shared with Ore

Define a canvas, named `areas` and optional `pagination` under menu `ui.layout` or global `menu.ui.layout`. Ordinary buttons require `ui.placement`; products use `ui.products.placement` unless overridden. In Search/Favourite screens the root result-slot count still limits source results, regardless of how many cards a graphical area could hold.

See [📐 Graphical layout - Premium](/menus-getting-started/ui-layout.md) for the complete schema and correct scopes. ArcMenu does not require Ore's generated pack merely to display its own controls; follow the ArcMenu integration's client setup. The `/shop dialogpack` command concerns **Ore assets**.

## Troubleshooting

If Inventory opens, check the two ArcMenu switches, plugin integration, resource setup and supported menu type. Item Sell and Sell All require physical inventories; Buy More uses ArcMenu product details instead of a separate Inventory-style ArcMenu screen. Use [Menu troubleshooting](/advanced-menus-and-support/troubleshooting.md) for symptoms.

[🎨 Presentation selection](/menu-ui-modes/ui-overview.md) · [📐 Layout - Premium](/menus-getting-started/ui-layout.md) · [🪨 Ore - Premium](/menu-ui-modes/ore-menus-premium.md).

true hides this particular Form button

This is separate from display-item.bedrock.*. The menu-level default is bedrock.click-event, and the global default is menu.bedrock.click-event. Trade availability, product conditions and click bindings still apply.

# Bedrock Form UI - Premium

Bedrock Form displays ordinary menu buttons as a **list**, with dedicated product information and quantity input forms. The same products, prices and click rules are shared with Java interfaces; Form does **not** use Ore/ArcMenu graphical coordinates.

## Enable Form

In `config.yml`:

```yaml
menu:
bedrock:
enabled: true
check-method: FLOODGATE
not-auto-close: true
auto-add-icon:
enabled: true
format: 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/InventivetalentDev/minecraft-assets/refs/heads/{version}/assets/minecraft/textures/{path}.png'
price-extra-line:
default: '{lang}'
only-buy: '{lang}'
only-sell: '{lang}'
```

In a menu file:

```yaml
title: '&8Farming'
size: 9
layout:
- '0000A0000'
bedrock:
enabled: true
content: '&7Choose a category'
buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: WHEAT
name: '&aFarming'
actions:
1:
type: shop_menu
shop: farming
```

Both the global and menu `bedrock.enabled` switches must allow Form. The server needs a supported Bedrock/Floodgate integration and the Premium functionality. If Form cannot be used, the usual Inventory interface is available.

## Set a custom button icon or second line

These keys belong **inside the active `display-item`**, not the root `ui` or the product's `bedrock.click-event`:

```yaml
buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: WHEAT
name: '&aFarming'
bedrock:
icon: 'path;;textures/items/wheat.png'
extra-line: '&7Seeds, crops and food'
hide: false
actions:
1:
type: shop_menu
shop: farming
```

| `display-item.bedrock` field | Meaning |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `icon` | `path;;` or `url;;
` |
| `extra-line` | Additional button line; price placeholders are supported for products |
| `hide` | `true` hides this particular Form button |

A `path;;` texture must exist **in the Bedrock client's resources**, not on the server disk. A `url;;` icon must be reachable by that client. Conditional display items should put icon settings on each intended variant.

Without an explicit icon, `menu.bedrock.auto-add-icon.enabled: true` attempts to resolve the vanilla material texture using its URL format. This does not resolve Java custom model data automatically. A button with an empty name, or `bedrock.hide: true`, can be omitted from the Form list.

## Product prices and click behavior

The price/extra line for products reads the active `display-item.bedrock.extra-line` first. Otherwise it uses the menu's `bedrock.price-extra-line` and then global `menu.bedrock.price-extra-line`:

```yaml
bedrock:
price-extra-line:
default: '&7Buy: {buy-price} | Sell: {sell-price}'
only-buy: '&7Buy: {buy-price}'
only-sell: '&7Sell: {sell-price}'
```

Set `display-item.bedrock.extra-line: ''` for an intentionally blank supplemental line. `{lang}` can use the matching language override.

A shop product normally opens an information Form. To execute an action directly instead, set the product-level shortcut in the **shop file**:

```yaml
items:
A:
bedrock:
click-event: buy
```

This is separate from `display-item.bedrock.*`. The menu-level default is `bedrock.click-event`, and the global default is `menu.bedrock.click-event`. Trade availability, product conditions and click bindings still apply.

## Form configuration reference

Native Form defaults live under global `menu.bedrock`; override supported values with menu `bedrock`, except options read globally such as player detection.

| Key relative to `bedrock` | Effect |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `enabled` | Allow Form for this menu |
| `content` | Menu description, root `content` as fallback |
| `check-method` | Global Bedrock-player detection method, e.g. `FLOODGATE` |
| `not-auto-close` | Reopen after supported information Form operations |
| `auto-add-icon.enabled` | Attempt vanilla material icons |
| `auto-add-icon.format` | URL template using `{version}` and `{path}` |
| `price-extra-line.default/only-buy/only-sell` | Product supplemental price text |
| `click-event` | Default direct shop-product action |
| `info.title` | Product information title |
| `info.buttons.buy/sell/buy-more/sell-all/back` | Information actions |
| `buy-or-sell.title` | Quantity input form title |
| `buy-or-sell.buttons.amount.name/tip` | Quantity input label and hint |
| `search.input`, `search.buttons.search` | Search form text |
| `favourite-edit.title/content`, `favourite-edit.buttons.*` | Favourite editing form text |

The generated product action buttons come from available click bindings, **not** from graphical `ui.products.actions`. Form quantity input does not reuse the Inventory Buy More button grid.

## Visibility and related menus

```yaml
menu-visibility:
form: false
```

Put this at the button or product root to hide only that entry in Form. Unspecified presentations default to visible. Form uses entries from the menu's root `layout` but ignores empty chest-grid spacing; decorative fillers usually should be hidden.

Search and Favourite have dedicated Form flows and reuse their data from the corresponding menu files. Physical Item Sell and Sell All remain Inventory screens.

# Native Dialog UI - Premium

Native Dialog uses the supported Paper Dialog API to display menus as actions or item lists. It is different from [🪨 Ore - Premium](/menu-ui-modes/ore-menus-premium.md), which is a graphical renderer built on Dialog.

## Enable native Dialog

Enable the capability in `config.yml`:

```yaml
menu:
dialog:
enabled: true
not-auto-close: true
auto-add-sprite:
enabled: true
auto-hide: true
format: ''
```

In your **menu**:

```yaml
title: '&8Categories'
size: 9
layout:
- '0000A0000'
dialog:
enabled: true
layout: multi-action
content: '&7Choose a category'
button-width: 150
columns: 2
buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: WHEAT
name: '&aFarming'
actions:
1:
type: shop_menu
shop: farming
```

Both global `menu.dialog.enabled` and menu `dialog.enabled` must be enabled. The server needs a supported Paper Dialog API and the Premium functionality. Java ArcMenu takes precedence if enabled and available; otherwise Dialog is attempted before Inventory.

## Choose a Dialog layout

| Menu `dialog.layout` | Result |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `multi-action` | Native Dialog action buttons |
| `item-action-list` | Native item-based action list |
| `ore` | Switch to the *graphical Ore renderer*, configured separately through `ui` |

The root `layout` identifies source entries; empty Inventory slots do not become empty Dialog rows. One entry can override its native action/list behavior with `buttons..dialog.layout`. Hide an item in one presentation with `menu-visibility`.

To suppress a material sprite on a particular button:

```yaml
buttons:
A:
dialog:
show-sprite: false
display-item:
material: WHEAT
name: '&aFarming'
actions:
1:
type: shop_menu
shop: farming
```

This is **button `dialog.show-sprite`**, not `ui.show-sprite` or `display-item.dialog.show-sprite`.

## Native Dialog configuration

Global defaults are under `menu.dialog`, with supported menu overrides under `dialog`:

| Key relative to `dialog` | Effect |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `enabled` | Allow Dialog on this menu |
| `layout` | `multi-action`, `item-action-list` or `ore` |
| `content` | Dialog body, falling back to root `content` |
| `button-width` | Native action width |
| `columns` | Native multi-action column count |
| `not-auto-close` | Supported information actions can keep the Dialog open |
| `auto-add-sprite.enabled/auto-hide/format` | Global material sprite behavior |
| `default-button` | Fallback exit-action label |
| `details` | Ore product details label |
| `info.display-item`, `info.title` | Product information display |
| `info.buttons.buy/sell/buy-more/sell-all/back` | Product information action labels |
| `buy-more.display-item/title/input/buttons.confirm` | Native quantity input flow |
| `search.input`, `search.buttons.search` | Search text input and submit |
| `favourite-edit.title/content/buttons.*` | Favourite editing controls |

Some sprite/resource settings are read globally; changing them on one menu may not affect resource generation. Labels can use language placeholders.

## Product actions and quantity

A product's native Dialog information controls come from its available click bindings and trade eligibility. **`ui.products.actions` only configures graphical Ore/ArcMenu controls**; it does not determine native Dialog buttons.

Quantity selection uses a native numeric input when `select-amount` is available and the product supports Buy More. Inventory Buy More slot controls are not displayed inside Dialog. A product retains its default buy/sell amount until a different quantity is selected.

Native Search provides keyword input and results; Favourite supports normal and editing screens. Neither reproduces Inventory item-input slots as native widget slots.

## Switching to Ore

Set **menu `dialog.layout: ore`** and configure its canvas and entry placements under `ui`. The graphical Ore renderer also needs its resource pack. Do not place native Dialog `layout` or `button-width` under `ui.renderers.dialog`.

[🪨 Ore - Premium](/menu-ui-modes/ore-menus-premium.md) · [🎨 Presentation selection](/menu-ui-modes/ui-overview.md) · [🔍 Search - Premium](/menu-types/search-menus-premium.md) · [❤️ Favourite - Premium](/menu-types/favourite-menus-premium.md).

# Inventory UI

Inventory is the normal chest-style menu. Its rows come from the **root** `layout` and `size`; `ui.layout` does not affect it.

## Open Inventory instead of Dialog / ArcMenu / Form

For a Java menu, disable its Dialog and ArcMenu choices (or disable those presentations globally):

```yaml
dialog:
enabled: false
arcmenu:
enabled: false
```

If Bedrock players must also receive Inventory instead of Form, disable their Form choice:

```yaml
bedrock:
enabled: false
```

These blocks belong at the **menu root**. Global equivalents are `menu.dialog.enabled`, `menu.arcmenu.enabled` and `menu.bedrock.enabled` in `config.yml`. There is **no** `ui.mode.java: inventory` setting.

## Working Inventory example

Save as `menus/common_menus/categories.yml`:

```yaml
title: '&8Categories'
size: 18
layout:
- '000000000'
- '000A0X000'
buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: WHEAT
name: '&aFarming'
actions:
1:
type: shop_menu
shop: farming
X:
display-item:
material: BARRIER
name: '&cClose'
actions:
1:
type: close
```

Create the `farming` shop before opening this example. Reload with `/shop reload` and open with `/shop menu categories`. Each row has nine slots; `0` is empty until you define `buttons.0`.

## How Inventory handles items

* `buttons.` describes a navigation/action button. Shop menus additionally resolve product IDs from the shop.
* `layout` controls order and slots. `ui.placement` does **not** move Inventory items.
* `menu-visibility.inventory: false` hides a button or product here without hiding it in Form/Ore/ArcMenu.
* `display-conditions` control whether an entry is available to a player.
* `menu.click-event` and product-specific click bindings govern product actions. Ordinary buttons use `actions`.

See [Layout and buttons](/menus-getting-started/layout-and-buttons.md) for markers and [Conditional display - Premium](/advanced-menus-and-support/conditional-display-premium.md) for dynamic entries.

## Refresh, titles and deposit screens

`menu.menu-update.circle-update` and `click-update` control item refresh. `menu.title-update.*` contains optional title update behavior. Avoid frequent refresh if the contents rarely change.

[Item Sell](/menu-types/item-sell-menus.md) and [Sell All](/menu-types/sell-all-menu.md) are physical Inventory screens. [Buy More](/menu-types/buy-more-menus.md) has a dedicated Inventory quantity selection layout.

## If Inventory opens unexpectedly

Check the global *and* menu-level switches, runtime integration availability and whether the requested menu type supports the chosen presentation. An empty Inventory slot usually means a missing layout marker, a missing entry, a failed display condition or `menu-visibility.inventory: false`.

[Presentation guide](/menu-ui-modes/ui-overview.md) · [Menu troubleshooting](/advanced-menus-and-support/troubleshooting.md).

🖥️Menu UI Modes

🪨Ore UI - Premium

Ore draws graphical cards and controls using the supported Paper Dialog API and a generated client resource pack. It shares graphical canvas/area settings with ArcMenu, but it is selected through dialog.layout: ore, not ui.mode.

Quick start

In config.yml:

Copy

menu:
dialog:
enabled: true
ore:
show-item-icon:
enabled: true
auto-hide-one: true
pack-format: 0

In menus/common_menus/categories.yml (the global menu.ui defaults provide the canvas and named sidebar area):

Copy

title: '&8Categories'
size: 9
layout:
- '0000A0000'
dialog:
enabled: true
layout: ore
content: '&7Browse categories'
buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: WHEAT
name: '&aFarming'
actions:
1:
type: shop_menu
shop: farming
ui:
appearance: button
placement:
area: sidebar
order: 0

The farming shop must exist. Reload, run /shop dialogpack and make sure clients load the newly generated pack. For a graphical shop menu, configure ui.products.placement as well; see 📐 Graphical layout - Premium.

What Ore reads

Key

Purpose

dialog.enabled / global menu.dialog.enabled

Allow the Dialog renderer

dialog.layout: ore

Choose Ore

dialog.content

Header content (root content fallback)

ui.layout.canvas/header/areas/pagination

Logical graphical screen and areas

ui.products.placement/card/price/actions

Graphical product cards and controls

Entry ui.placement

Where ordinary buttons or specific products appear

Entry ui.appearance

Graphical button/card style

ui.theme

Shared graphic colors

ui.renderers.ore.templates

Generated background/selected-state assets

Global menu.dialog.ore.show-item-icon.*

Icon generation and quantity label behavior

Global menu.dialog.ore.pack-format

Resource-pack format selection

The root Inventory layout remains useful to identify entries and special result markers, but its chest coordinates do not translate to pixels. Navigation buttons must have graphical placements. Product cards use ui.products.placement unless a specific product supplies its own ui.placement.

Customize a graphical card texture

Put PNGs under plugins/UltimateShop/textures/shop/, then add:

This is graphical ui.renderers.ore.templates. Source PNG paths must be relative; do not use absolute filesystem paths or ... Colors should be quoted RGB strings. Shared layout/card/theme keys may take precedence over template geometry and base styling.

Layout and text constraints

Prefer vertical coordinates/heights divisible by 9; put cards in an area tall enough for them.

Cards need enough height for icon, name, descriptions and operation buttons; undersized or overlapping entries can fail validation.

ui.products.card.lore-lines limits lore shown in Ore card bodies; longer information can remain in tooltips.

Material names may be client-translated; the server cannot measure every translated string's final width precisely.

ArcMenu-specific font scaling does not imply the same rendered size in Ore.

Check Graphical layout - Premium for bounds, grids, stacks, free placement and pagination.

Generate and distribute the pack

Run /shop dialogpack after changing Ore layout, theme, templates or related icons.

Find the generated output under plugins/UltimateShop/pack/.

Serve the resulting resource pack to players and verify that the client accepted it.

Reopen the menu to verify the actual layout.

/shop dialogpack <format> can override the pack format when needed. A regular /shop reload updates server-side YAML but does not ensure that the client downloaded new assets.

If you see Inventory instead, check both Dialog switches, the supported API/runtime, the menu's dialog.layout and console layout/pack errors. If cards overlap, validate graphical areas before regenerating again.

# Ore UI - Premium

Ore draws graphical cards and controls using the supported Paper Dialog API and a generated client resource pack. It shares graphical canvas/area settings with ArcMenu, but it is **selected through `dialog.layout: ore`**, not `ui.mode`.

## Quick start

In `config.yml`:

```yaml
menu:
dialog:
enabled: true
ore:
show-item-icon:
enabled: true
auto-hide-one: true
pack-format: 0
```

In `menus/common_menus/categories.yml` (the global `menu.ui` defaults provide the canvas and named `sidebar` area):

```yaml
title: '&8Categories'
size: 9
layout:
- '0000A0000'
dialog:
enabled: true
layout: ore
content: '&7Browse categories'
buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: WHEAT
name: '&aFarming'
actions:
1:
type: shop_menu
shop: farming
ui:
appearance: button
placement:
area: sidebar
order: 0
```

The `farming` shop must exist. Reload, run `/shop dialogpack` and make sure clients **load the newly generated pack**. For a graphical **shop** menu, configure `ui.products.placement` as well; see [📐 Graphical layout - Premium](/menus-getting-started/ui-layout.md).

## What Ore reads

| Key | Purpose |
| ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `dialog.enabled` / global `menu.dialog.enabled` | Allow the Dialog renderer |
| `dialog.layout: ore` | Choose Ore |
| `dialog.content` | Header content (root `content` fallback) |
| `ui.layout.canvas/header/areas/pagination` | Logical graphical screen and areas |
| `ui.products.placement/card/price/actions` | Graphical product cards and controls |
| Entry `ui.placement` | Where ordinary buttons or specific products appear |
| Entry `ui.appearance` | Graphical button/card style |
| `ui.theme` | Shared graphic colors |
| `ui.renderers.ore.templates` | Generated background/selected-state assets |
| Global `menu.dialog.ore.show-item-icon.*` | Icon generation and quantity label behavior |
| Global `menu.dialog.ore.pack-format` | Resource-pack format selection |

The root Inventory `layout` remains useful to identify entries and special result markers, but its chest coordinates do **not** translate to pixels. Navigation buttons must have graphical placements. Product cards use `ui.products.placement` unless a specific product supplies its own `ui.placement`.

## Customize a graphical card texture

Put PNGs under `plugins/UltimateShop/textures/shop/`, then add:

```yaml
ui:
renderers:
ore:
templates:
product:
texture: 'shop/card.png'
selected-texture: 'shop/card-selected.png'
selected-background: '#244A32'
selected-border: '#65D98B'
```

This is **graphical** `ui.renderers.ore.templates`. Source PNG paths must be relative; do not use absolute filesystem paths or `..`. Colors should be quoted RGB strings. Shared layout/card/theme keys may take precedence over template geometry and base styling.

## Layout and text constraints

* Prefer vertical coordinates/heights divisible by 9; put cards in an area tall enough for them.
* Cards need enough height for icon, name, descriptions and operation buttons; undersized or overlapping entries can fail validation.
* `ui.products.card.lore-lines` limits lore shown in Ore card bodies; longer information can remain in tooltips.
* Material names may be client-translated; the server cannot measure every translated string's final width precisely.
* ArcMenu-specific font scaling does not imply the same rendered size in Ore.

Check [Graphical layout - Premium](/menus-getting-started/ui-layout.md) for bounds, grids, stacks, free placement and pagination.

## Generate and distribute the pack

1. Run `/shop dialogpack` after changing Ore layout, theme, templates or related icons.
2. Find the generated output under `plugins/UltimateShop/pack/`.
3. Serve the resulting resource pack to players and verify that the client accepted it.
4. Reopen the menu to verify the actual layout.

`/shop dialogpack ` can override the pack format when needed. A regular `/shop reload` updates server-side YAML but **does not ensure that the client downloaded new assets**.

If you see Inventory instead, check both Dialog switches, the supported API/runtime, the menu's `dialog.layout` and console layout/pack errors. If cards overlap, validate graphical areas before regenerating again.

[📐 Graphical layout - Premium](/menus-getting-started/ui-layout.md) · [💬 Native Dialog - Premium](/menu-ui-modes/dialog-menus-premium.md) · [🩺 Troubleshooting](/advanced-menus-and-support/troubleshooting.md).

🖥️Menu UI Modes

🎨UI Modes Overview

A presentation is the client interface used to show an existing Common, Shop, Search or Favourite menu. It does not change product prices, click bindings, conditions or data storage.

Choose with native switches, not ui.mode

In config.yml, enable the presentations that the server should support:

Copy

menu:
dialog:
enabled: true
bedrock:
enabled: true
arcmenu:
enabled: false

In an individual menu, choose the layout and enable its intended presentations:

Copy

title: '&8Farming'
size: 9
layout:
- '0000A0000'
dialog:
enabled: true
layout: ore
content: '&7Browse our products'
bedrock:
enabled: true
content: '&7Browse our products'
arcmenu:
enabled: false

Inventory

Inventory is the fallback when another presentation is disabled or unavailable. It has no additional edition requirement beyond the menu itself.

Bedrock Form - Premium

Bedrock Form - Premium requires global menu.bedrock.enabled and menu bedrock.enabled, with a supported Bedrock/Floodgate integration.

Native Dialog - Premium

Native Dialog - Premium requires global menu.dialog.enabled, menu dialog.enabled and a supported Paper Dialog API. Set dialog.layout to multi-action or item-action-list.

Ore - Premium

Ore - Premium requires global/menu Dialog enabled, dialog.layout: ore, supported Paper and a generated client resource pack.

ArcMenu - Premium

ArcMenu - Premium requires global menu.arcmenu.enabled, menu arcmenu.enabled and a compatible ArcMenu integration.

When a menu omits dialog.enabled or bedrock.enabled, it defaults to true. ArcMenu is opt-in: its menu switch defaults to false.

Java priority

ArcMenu → Dialog / Ore → Inventory. If ArcMenu fails to open, the normal menu-opening flow can try Dialog/Ore when enabled and supported. If neither graphical/native route applies, Inventory is used. Bedrock Form is selected separately for Bedrock players.

dialog.layout is a menu-level selector: multi-action, item-action-list or ore. It does not configure pixel coordinates.

Where does each configuration belong?

What you want to change

Correct key

Inventory rows and buttons

Root size, layout, buttons

Native Dialog mode, text and controls

Menu dialog.*, global menu.dialog.*

Bedrock Form enablement, button text and icons

Menu bedrock.*, global menu.bedrock.*, display-item.bedrock.*

ArcMenu enablement

menu.arcmenu.enabled and menu arcmenu.enabled

Ore/ArcMenu coordinates and card appearance

menu.ui.* and menu ui.*

Show or hide a product in one presentation

Entry menu-visibility.<presentation>

ui.mode, ui.visible-in, ui.show-sprite and native Form/Dialog ui.renderers fields are not supported. The ui section is reserved for graphical drawing and placement.

Menus that need a physical inventory

Item Sell and Sell All use a real Inventory container, even when opened from another type of screen. Inventory Buy More buttons are not automatically converted into Form or Dialog widgets; see Buy More.

Related: Configuration scopes · Graphical layout - Premium · Troubleshooting.

# UI Modes Overview

A **presentation** is the client interface used to show an existing Common, Shop, Search or Favourite menu. It does not change product prices, click bindings, conditions or data storage.

## Choose with native switches, not `ui.mode`

In `config.yml`, enable the presentations that the server should support:

```yaml
menu:
dialog:
enabled: true
bedrock:
enabled: true
arcmenu:
enabled: false
```

In an individual menu, choose the layout and enable its intended presentations:

```yaml
title: '&8Farming'
size: 9
layout:
- '0000A0000'
dialog:
enabled: true
layout: ore
content: '&7Browse our products'
bedrock:
enabled: true
content: '&7Browse our products'
arcmenu:
enabled: false
```

### Inventory

[Inventory](/menu-ui-modes/inventory-ui.md) is the fallback when another presentation is disabled or unavailable. It has no additional edition requirement beyond the menu itself.

### Bedrock Form - Premium

[Bedrock Form - Premium](/menu-ui-modes/bedrock-menus-premium.md) requires global `menu.bedrock.enabled` and menu `bedrock.enabled`, with a supported Bedrock/Floodgate integration.

### Native Dialog - Premium

[Native Dialog - Premium](/menu-ui-modes/dialog-menus-premium.md) requires global `menu.dialog.enabled`, menu `dialog.enabled` and a supported Paper Dialog API. Set `dialog.layout` to `multi-action` or `item-action-list`.

### Ore - Premium

[Ore - Premium](/menu-ui-modes/ore-menus-premium.md) requires global/menu Dialog enabled, `dialog.layout: ore`, supported Paper and a generated client resource pack.

### ArcMenu - Premium

[ArcMenu - Premium](/menu-ui-modes/arcmenu-menus-premium.md) requires global `menu.arcmenu.enabled`, menu `arcmenu.enabled` and a compatible ArcMenu integration.

When a menu omits `dialog.enabled` or `bedrock.enabled`, it defaults to `true`. ArcMenu is **opt-in**: its menu switch defaults to `false`.

### Java priority

**ArcMenu → Dialog / Ore → Inventory.** If ArcMenu fails to open, the normal menu-opening flow can try Dialog/Ore when enabled and supported. If neither graphical/native route applies, Inventory is used. Bedrock Form is selected separately for Bedrock players.

`dialog.layout` is a *menu-level selector*: `multi-action`, `item-action-list` or `ore`. It does not configure pixel coordinates.

## Where does each configuration belong?

| What you want to change | Correct key |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Inventory rows and buttons | Root `size`, `layout`, `buttons` |
| Native Dialog mode, text and controls | Menu `dialog.*`, global `menu.dialog.*` |
| Bedrock Form enablement, button text and icons | Menu `bedrock.*`, global `menu.bedrock.*`, `display-item.bedrock.*` |
| ArcMenu enablement | `menu.arcmenu.enabled` and menu `arcmenu.enabled` |
| Ore/ArcMenu coordinates and card appearance | `menu.ui.*` and menu `ui.*` |
| Show or hide a product in one presentation | Entry `menu-visibility.
` |

`ui.mode`, `ui.visible-in`, `ui.show-sprite` and native Form/Dialog `ui.renderers` fields are **not supported**. The `ui` section is reserved for graphical drawing and placement.

## Menus that need a physical inventory

Item Sell and Sell All use a real Inventory container, even when opened from another type of screen. Inventory Buy More buttons are not automatically converted into Form or Dialog widgets; see [Buy More](/menu-types/buy-more-menus.md).

Related: [Configuration scopes](/menus-getting-started/menu-configuration.md) · [Graphical layout - Premium](/menus-getting-started/ui-layout.md) · [Troubleshooting](/advanced-menus-and-support/troubleshooting.md).

🧱Layout & Buttons

Basic Layout

UltimateShop uses layout to define menu slots and buttons to configure regular menu buttons. Shop menus can also reference shop products and shop-specific buttons directly in their layouts.

This guide covers Inventory slot layouts, button configuration, and display rules. For graphical positioning in Ore and ArcMenu, see Graphical UI Layout.

Basic Example

A common menu typically consists of three main sections: size, layout, and buttons.

Copy

title: '&8Main Menu'
size: 18

layout:
- '000000000'
- '000A0X000'

buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: WHEAT
name: '&aFarming'

actions:
1:
type: shop_menu
shop: farming

X:
display-item:
material: BARRIER
name: '&cClose'

actions:
1:
type: close

Save this configuration as menus/common_menus/main.yml. After reloading the plugin, open the menu using /shop menu main.

Slot Layout

The example above creates an Inventory menu with 18 slots arranged in two rows.

First row:

Second row:

Here, A and X reference buttons.A and buttons.X. The remaining positions are empty unless matching entries are defined.

Option

Description

title

Menu title

size

Number of Inventory slots

layout

Defines which entry ID occupies each slot

buttons

Defines regular button appearances and click actions

Supported Inventory sizes are 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, and 54, with nine slots per row.

Layout Characters and IDs

The layout section uses strings to represent slots. Entries are read from left to right, then from top to bottom.

Single-Character IDs

By default, each character represents one slot.

For example:

This layout contains nine slots. A, B, C, D, and E reference their corresponding buttons or products.

Keep the following rules in mind:

IDs are case-sensitive. A and a are different IDs.

The same ID can appear in multiple slots.

An ID without a matching entry does not create a button.

0 is a regular ID, not a reserved empty-slot marker.

For example:

Every slot marked with 0 will display a gray stained glass pane.

If no matching 0 entry exists, those slots normally remain empty.

Multi-Character IDs

To use an ID containing multiple characters, enclose it in backticks within the layout string. The entire ID will occupy a single slot.

For example:

This produces the following nine slots:

The corresponding buttons can use their full IDs:

Backticks are only used to identify multi-character IDs inside layout. They are not part of the IDs themselves.

Each layout row should resolve to nine slots to avoid shifting subsequent entries into unexpected positions.

Regular Buttons and Shop Products

A layout can reference different types of entries depending on the menu type.

Common Menu Buttons

Common menus define their buttons directly under the buttons section of the menu file.

For example:

Here, A references buttons.A.

Buttons can open other menus, open shops, close menus, or perform other supported actions.

Shop Menu Entries

Shop menus can display both products and regular buttons.

For example, in menus/shop_menu_templates/default.yml:

In shops/farming.yml:

The resulting layout contains:

ID

Source

Purpose

A

shops/farming.yml → items.A

Displays the wheat product

X

menus/shop_menu_templates/default.yml → buttons.X

Displays the back button

Shop files can also define shop-specific regular buttons under their own buttons section.

Therefore, a shop layout can reference shop products, shop-specific buttons, and buttons defined in the menu template.

Avoid using the same ID for different entry types. When IDs conflict, UltimateShop selects an entry according to its internal lookup priority rather than displaying multiple entries in the same slot.

Button Configuration

Each regular button can define its display item, click actions, conditions, and presentation-specific options.

Available Options

Option

Description

display-item

Display item, name, and other item properties

actions

Actions executed when the button is clicked

fail-actions

Actions executed when click conditions are not met

conditions

Conditions required to execute click actions

display-conditions

Conditions required for the button to appear (Premium)

menu-visibility

Controls visibility in different menu presentations

dialog.layout

Overrides the Dialog presentation style for an individual button

dialog.show-sprite

Controls whether a Dialog item sprite is displayed

ui

Graphical appearance and placement for Ore and ArcMenu

Click Actions and Conditions

Use actions to define what happens when a player clicks a button.

For example:

When a player clicks the button, UltimateShop checks conditions first:

If the conditions are met, actions are executed.

If the conditions are not met, fail-actions are executed.

The conditions section controls click behavior. It does not automatically hide the button.

Display Conditions - Premium

Use display-conditions when a button should only appear if certain requirements are met.

For example:

This button is only eligible to appear when the player has the shop.vip permission.

display-conditions and conditions serve different purposes:

Option

Purpose

display-conditions

Determines whether the button appears

conditions

Determines whether clicking the button successfully executes its actions

If display conditions depend on permissions, placeholders, or other player-specific states, enable dynamic-layout so the layout can be evaluated for each player.

Dynamic Layout - Premium

Dynamic layouts allow a slot to display different entries depending on the player's state.

For example:

The backtick-enclosed expression A||B defines multiple candidates for a single slot.

UltimateShop evaluates the candidates from left to right:

If A exists and satisfies its display conditions, display A.

Otherwise, check B.

If B satisfies its display conditions, display B.

If no candidate is available, leave the slot empty.

As a result, players with the shop.vip permission see VIP Shop, while other players see Normal Shop.

Multiple candidate IDs can be separated using ||. The entire expression still occupies only one slot.

When dynamic-layout is enabled, layout IDs can also contain PlaceholderAPI placeholders, allowing entries to be resolved dynamically for each player.

Buttons in Different Menu Presentations

The same button can be used in Inventory, Bedrock Form, Dialog, Ore, and ArcMenu. However, these presentations do not use identical layout systems.

Presentation Visibility

Use menu-visibility to control which presentations can display a button.

For example:

Option

Presentation

inventory

Inventory

form

Bedrock Form

dialog

Native Dialog

item-action-list

Dialog Item Action List

ore

Ore

arcmenu

ArcMenu

Presentations are visible by default when their visibility options are not specified.

If ore or item-action-list is not explicitly configured, it uses menu-visibility.dialog as its fallback.

Layout Behavior by Presentation

Presentation

Layout Behavior

Inventory

Uses the root layout to determine slot positions

Bedrock Form

Builds a list from menu entries

Dialog

Builds action buttons or item lists from menu entries

Ore

Uses ui.layout and ui.placement for graphical positioning

ArcMenu

Uses ui.layout and ui.placement for graphical positioning

Inventory slot positions are not automatically converted into Ore or ArcMenu graphical coordinates.

For example:

In Ore and ArcMenu, ui.placement determines the graphical area and ordering of the button.

A regular button with an explicit ui.placement can also become a graphical menu entry even if its ID does not appear in the root layout.

Products can inherit their default graphical placement from the menu's ui.products.placement.

menu-visibility determines whether an entry is allowed to appear in a presentation, while ui.placement determines where it appears in graphical interfaces. These settings serve different purposes.

For canvas dimensions, named areas, grids, and graphical coordinates, see Graphical UI Layout.

# Layout & Buttons

## Basic Layout

UltimateShop uses `layout` to define menu slots and `buttons` to configure regular menu buttons. Shop menus can also reference shop products and shop-specific buttons directly in their layouts.

This guide covers Inventory slot layouts, button configuration, and display rules. For graphical positioning in Ore and ArcMenu, see [Graphical UI Layout](/menus-getting-started/ui-layout.md).

### Basic Example

A common menu typically consists of three main sections: `size`, `layout`, and `buttons`.

```yaml
title: '&8Main Menu'
size: 18

layout:
- '000000000'
- '000A0X000'

buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: WHEAT
name: '&aFarming'

actions:
1:
type: shop_menu
shop: farming

X:
display-item:
material: BARRIER
name: '&cClose'

actions:
1:
type: close
```

Save this configuration as `menus/common_menus/main.yml`. After reloading the plugin, open the menu using `/shop menu main`.

### Slot Layout

The example above creates an Inventory menu with 18 slots arranged in two rows.

**First row:**

```
0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0
```

**Second row:**

```
0 0 0 A 0 X 0 0 0
```

Here, `A` and `X` reference `buttons.A` and `buttons.X`. The remaining positions are empty unless matching entries are defined.

| Option | Description |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `title` | Menu title |
| `size` | Number of Inventory slots |
| `layout` | Defines which entry ID occupies each slot |
| `buttons` | Defines regular button appearances and click actions |

Supported Inventory sizes are `9`, `18`, `27`, `36`, `45`, and `54`, with nine slots per row.

## Layout Characters and IDs

The `layout` section uses strings to represent slots. Entries are read from left to right, then from top to bottom.

### Single-Character IDs

By default, each character represents one slot.

For example:

```yaml
layout:
- 'A0B0C0D0E'
```

This layout contains nine slots. `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, and `E` reference their corresponding buttons or products.

Keep the following rules in mind:

* IDs are case-sensitive. `A` and `a` are different IDs.
* The same ID can appear in multiple slots.
* An ID without a matching entry does not create a button.
* `0` is a regular ID, not a reserved empty-slot marker.

For example:

```yaml
layout:
- '000000000'

buttons:
'0':
display-item:
material: GRAY_STAINED_GLASS_PANE
name: ' '
```

Every slot marked with `0` will display a gray stained glass pane.

If no matching `0` entry exists, those slots normally remain empty.

### Multi-Character IDs

To use an ID containing multiple characters, enclose it in backticks within the layout string. The entire ID will occupy a single slot.

For example:

```yaml
layout:
- '0`food_buy``food_sell`000000'
```

This produces the following nine slots:

```
0 | food_buy | food_sell | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0
```

The corresponding buttons can use their full IDs:

```
buttons:
food_buy:
display-item:
material: EMERALD
name: '&aBuy Food'

food_sell:
display-item:
material: GOLD_INGOT
name: '&eSell Food'
```

Backticks are only used to identify multi-character IDs inside `layout`. They are not part of the IDs themselves.

Each layout row should resolve to nine slots to avoid shifting subsequent entries into unexpected positions.

## Regular Buttons and Shop Products

A layout can reference different types of entries depending on the menu type.

### Common Menu Buttons

Common menus define their buttons directly under the `buttons` section of the menu file.

For example:

```yaml
layout:
- '0000A0000'

buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: CHEST
name: '&aOpen Shop'

actions:
1:
type: shop_menu
shop: farming
```

Here, `A` references `buttons.A`.

Buttons can open other menus, open shops, close menus, or perform other supported actions.

### Shop Menu Entries

Shop menus can display both products and regular buttons.

For example, in `menus/shop_menu_templates/default.yml`:

```yaml
title: '{shop-name}'
size: 9

layout:
- '0000A0X00'

buttons:
X:
display-item:
material: ARROW
name: '&eBack'

actions:
1:
type: back
```

In `shops/farming.yml`:

```yaml
settings:
menu: default

items:
A:
display-item:
material: WHEAT
name: '&eWheat'

products:
1:
material: WHEAT

buy-prices:
1:
economy-plugin: Vault
amount: 5
```

The resulting layout contains:

| ID | Source | Purpose |
| --- | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| `A` | `shops/farming.yml` → `items.A` | Displays the wheat product |
| `X` | `menus/shop_menu_templates/default.yml` → `buttons.X` | Displays the back button |

Shop files can also define shop-specific regular buttons under their own `buttons` section.

Therefore, a shop layout can reference shop products, shop-specific buttons, and buttons defined in the menu template.

Avoid using the same ID for different entry types. When IDs conflict, UltimateShop selects an entry according to its internal lookup priority rather than displaying multiple entries in the same slot.

## Button Configuration

Each regular button can define its display item, click actions, conditions, and presentation-specific options.

### Available Options

| Option | Description |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `display-item` | Display item, name, and other item properties |
| `actions` | Actions executed when the button is clicked |
| `fail-actions` | Actions executed when click conditions are not met |
| `conditions` | Conditions required to execute click actions |
| `display-conditions` | Conditions required for the button to appear (Premium) |
| `menu-visibility` | Controls visibility in different menu presentations |
| `dialog.layout` | Overrides the Dialog presentation style for an individual button |
| `dialog.show-sprite` | Controls whether a Dialog item sprite is displayed |
| `ui` | Graphical appearance and placement for Ore and ArcMenu |

### Click Actions and Conditions

Use `actions` to define what happens when a player clicks a button.

For example:

```yaml
buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: DIAMOND
name: '&bVIP Shop'

conditions:
1:
type: permission
permission: shop.vip

actions:
1:
type: shop_menu
shop: vip

fail-actions:
1:
type: message
message: '&cYou do not have permission!'
```

When a player clicks the button, UltimateShop checks `conditions` first:

* If the conditions are met, `actions` are executed.
* If the conditions are not met, `fail-actions` are executed.

The `conditions` section controls click behavior. It does not automatically hide the button.

### Display Conditions - Premium

Use `display-conditions` when a button should only appear if certain requirements are met.

For example:

```yaml
buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: DIAMOND
name: '&bVIP Shop'

display-conditions:
1:
type: permission
permission: shop.vip
```

This button is only eligible to appear when the player has the `shop.vip` permission.

`display-conditions` and `conditions` serve different purposes:

| Option | Purpose |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `display-conditions` | Determines whether the button appears |
| `conditions` | Determines whether clicking the button successfully executes its actions |

If display conditions depend on permissions, placeholders, or other player-specific states, enable `dynamic-layout` so the layout can be evaluated for each player.

### Dynamic Layout - Premium

Dynamic layouts allow a slot to display different entries depending on the player's state.

For example:

```yaml
dynamic-layout: true

layout:
- '000000000'
- '000`A||B`00000'

buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: DIAMOND
name: '&bVIP Shop'

display-conditions:
1:
type: permission
permission: shop.vip

actions:
1:
type: shop_menu
shop: vip

B:
display-item:
material: EMERALD
name: '&aNormal Shop'

actions:
1:
type: shop_menu
shop: normal
```

The backtick-enclosed expression `A||B` defines multiple candidates for a single slot.

UltimateShop evaluates the candidates from left to right:

1. If `A` exists and satisfies its display conditions, display `A`.
2. Otherwise, check `B`.
3. If `B` satisfies its display conditions, display `B`.
4. If no candidate is available, leave the slot empty.

As a result, players with the `shop.vip` permission see VIP Shop, while other players see Normal Shop.

Multiple candidate IDs can be separated using `||`. The entire expression still occupies only one slot.

When `dynamic-layout` is enabled, layout IDs can also contain PlaceholderAPI placeholders, allowing entries to be resolved dynamically for each player.

## Buttons in Different Menu Presentations

The same button can be used in Inventory, Bedrock Form, Dialog, Ore, and ArcMenu. However, these presentations do not use identical layout systems.

### Presentation Visibility

Use `menu-visibility` to control which presentations can display a button.

For example:

```yaml
buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: EMERALD
name: '&aExample'

menu-visibility:
inventory: true
form: true
dialog: true
item-action-list: false
ore: false
arcmenu: true
```

| Option | Presentation |
| ------------------ | ----------------------- |
| `inventory` | Inventory |
| `form` | Bedrock Form |
| `dialog` | Native Dialog |
| `item-action-list` | Dialog Item Action List |
| `ore` | Ore |
| `arcmenu` | ArcMenu |

Presentations are visible by default when their visibility options are not specified.

If `ore` or `item-action-list` is not explicitly configured, it uses `menu-visibility.dialog` as its fallback.

### Layout Behavior by Presentation

| Presentation | Layout Behavior |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Inventory | Uses the root `layout` to determine slot positions |
| Bedrock Form | Builds a list from menu entries |
| Dialog | Builds action buttons or item lists from menu entries |
| Ore | Uses `ui.layout` and `ui.placement` for graphical positioning |
| ArcMenu | Uses `ui.layout` and `ui.placement` for graphical positioning |

Inventory slot positions are not automatically converted into Ore or ArcMenu graphical coordinates.

For example:

```yaml
buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: EMERALD
name: '&aOpen Shop'

actions:
1:
type: shop_menu
shop: farming

ui:
appearance: button

placement:
area: sidebar
order: 0
```

In Ore and ArcMenu, `ui.placement` determines the graphical area and ordering of the button.

A regular button with an explicit `ui.placement` can also become a graphical menu entry even if its ID does not appear in the root `layout`.

Products can inherit their default graphical placement from the menu's `ui.products.placement`.

`menu-visibility` determines whether an entry is allowed to appear in a presentation, while `ui.placement` determines where it appears in graphical interfaces. These settings serve different purposes.

For canvas dimensions, named areas, grids, and graphical coordinates, see [Graphical UI Layout](/menus-getting-started/ui-layout.md).

# Menu Configuration & Inheritance

UltimateShop allows each menu to have its own configuration while also supporting shared menu templates across multiple shops.

Global settings provide common defaults, while individual menus and shops can override specific options without duplicating the entire configuration.

This guide explains how menu configurations are organized, inherited, and prioritized.

## Configuration Structure

Menu configurations are primarily stored in three locations:

```
plugins/UltimateShop/
│
├── config.yml
│ └── menu # Global menu settings
│
├── menus/
│ ├── common_menus/ # Common menus
│ ├── shop_menu_templates/ # Shop menu templates
│ ├── buy_more_menus/ # Amount selection menus
│ ├── search_menus/ # Search menus
│ ├── favourite_menus/ # Favourite menus
│ └── item_sell_menus/ # Item sell menus
│
└── shops/
├── farming.yml # Shop configuration
└── mining.yml
```

### Global Configuration (`config.yml`)

The `menu` section in `config.yml` controls global menu features and default settings.

For example:

```yaml
menu:
dialog:
enabled: true

bedrock:
enabled: true

arcmenu:
enabled: false

ui:
theme:
accent: '#65E8EF'
```

| Section | Description |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `menu.dialog` | Global settings for Dialog and Ore |
| `menu.bedrock` | Global settings for Bedrock Form |
| `menu.arcmenu` | Global settings for ArcMenu |
| `menu.ui` | Default graphical layout and appearance for Ore and ArcMenu |
| Other `menu.*` | Global features such as menu updates, click actions, search, and amount selection |

### Menu Configuration (`menus/`)

Each YAML file in the `menus` directory defines a menu, including its title, layout, buttons, and presentation settings.

For example, `menus/common_menus/main.yml`:

```yaml
title: '&8Main Menu'
size: 27

layout:
- '000000000'
- '0000A0000'
- '000000000'

dialog:
enabled: true
layout: multi-action

buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: EMERALD
name: '&aOpen Shop'

actions:
1:
type: shop_menu
shop: farming
```

Common menus use their own configuration files directly.

Shop menus can reference a shared template through `settings.menu`, allowing multiple shops to reuse the same menu structure.

### Shop Configuration (`shops/`)

Shop files define products and trading rules. They can also select a menu template or override its configuration.

For example, `shops/farming.yml`:

```yaml
settings:
menu: default

menu-settings:
title: '&aFarming Shop'

dialog:
layout: ore
```

* `settings.menu`: Specifies the menu template to use.
* `settings.menu-settings`: Overrides menu settings for this particular shop.

Multiple shops can share the same template while using different titles, layouts, or presentation settings through `menu-settings`.

### How Configurations Work Together

**Common Menu:**

```
config.yml
└── Global presentation settings
↓
menus/common_menus/main.yml
└── Individual menu settings
```

**Shop Menu:**

```
menus/shop_menu_templates/default.yml
│
▼
Load menu template
│
▼
shops/farming.yml
└── settings.menu-settings
│
▼
Override template settings
│
▼
config.yml → menu.ui
└── Fill missing graphical settings
│
▼
Final menu configuration
```

Only graphical `ui` settings use the recursive default-filling mechanism shown above. Dialog, Bedrock, and other global settings are resolved through their respective configuration lookup methods.

## Configuration Inheritance & Priority

UltimateShop uses different inheritance rules depending on the configuration type.

### Shop Menu Template Overrides

The `settings.menu-settings` section allows a shop to override specific settings from its menu template.

Suppose `menus/shop_menu_templates/default.yml` contains:

```
title: '&8Default Shop'

size: 27

layout:
- '000000000'
- '0000A0000'
- '000000000'

dialog:
enabled: true
layout: multi-action
columns: 2

ui:
products:
card:
icon-size: 32
padding: 9
```

In `shops/farming.yml`:

```
settings:
menu: default

menu-settings:
title: '&aFarming Shop'

dialog:
layout: ore

ui:
products:
card:
icon-size: 48
```

The resulting configuration is equivalent to:

```
title: '&aFarming Shop'

size: 27

layout:
- '000000000'
- '0000A0000'
- '000000000'

dialog:
enabled: true
layout: ore
columns: 2

ui:
products:
card:
icon-size: 48
padding: 9
```

**Merge Rules:**

| Situation | Result |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| An option is defined in the shop override | The shop's value takes priority |
| An option is missing from the shop override | The template's value is preserved |
| An option contains nested sections | Sections are merged recursively |
| An option contains a list | The entire list is replaced |

You only need to include the settings you want to change in `settings.menu-settings`.

If a shop does not specify `settings.menu` but provides `settings.menu-settings`, UltimateShop can also create its shop menu directly from those settings.

### Graphical UI Inheritance

Ore and ArcMenu use the `ui` section for graphical settings.

Global configuration:

```
menu:
ui:
products:
card:
icon-size: 32
padding: 9

theme:
background: '#141E30'
accent: '#65E8EF'
```

Individual menu configuration:

```
ui:
products:
card:
icon-size: 48

theme:
accent: '#FFAA00'
```

The resulting graphical configuration is:

```
ui:
products:
card:
icon-size: 48
padding: 9

theme:
background: '#141E30'
accent: '#FFAA00'
```

**Inheritance Rules:**

* Values explicitly defined in the menu take priority.
* Missing values are inherited from global `menu.ui`.
* Nested sections are filled recursively without overwriting existing values.
* Explicit `false` values, empty strings, and empty lists are preserved.

For shop menus, the processing order is:

**Menu Template → Shop Overrides → Global Graphical Defaults**

### Other Presentation Settings

Native settings for Dialog, Bedrock Form, and ArcMenu generally follow this lookup order:

1. Current menu configuration.
2. Global settings in `config.yml`.
3. Built-in fallback values.

For example:

```
# config.yml
menu:
dialog:
not-auto-close: true
```

An individual menu can override this setting:

```
dialog:
not-auto-close: false
```

In this case, the menu uses `false`.

However, **presentation enablement does not follow ordinary override behavior**. If a presentation is disabled globally, an individual menu cannot force-enable it with `enabled: true`.

Some settings are also read exclusively from the global configuration, such as Bedrock client detection and certain resource-pack generation options.

Menu content uses a separate fallback mechanism:

| Presentation | Content Lookup Order |
| ------------ | ----------------------------- |
| Dialog / Ore | `dialog.content` → `content` |
| Bedrock Form | `bedrock.content` → `content` |
| ArcMenu | `arcmenu.content` → `content` |

If neither value is configured, an empty string is used.

## Menu Presentation Selection

UltimateShop supports multiple presentations for the same menu content.

| Presentation | Global Setting | Menu Setting |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| 📦 Inventory | No additional enablement required | No additional enablement required |
| 💬 Dialog | `menu.dialog.enabled` | `dialog.enabled` |
| 🪨 Ore | `menu.dialog.enabled` | `dialog.enabled` + `dialog.layout: ore` |
| ✨ ArcMenu | `menu.arcmenu.enabled` | `arcmenu.enabled` |
| 🛏️ Bedrock Form | `menu.bedrock.enabled` | `bedrock.enabled` |

Dialog, Ore, ArcMenu, and Bedrock Form require the Premium edition and their respective runtime requirements.

### Java Client Priority

For menus that support these presentations, the selection priority is:

**ArcMenu → Dialog / Ore → Inventory**

Dialog and Ore are selected using `dialog.layout`:

| Value | Presentation |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------- |
| `multi-action` | Native Dialog action buttons |
| `item-action-list` | Native Dialog item list |
| `ore` | Ore graphical interface |

For example:

```
dialog:
enabled: true
layout: ore

arcmenu:
enabled: true
```

If both presentations are globally enabled and supported by the runtime, ArcMenu takes priority.

If ArcMenu cannot be used, UltimateShop can attempt Dialog/Ore. When no alternative presentation is available, Inventory is used.

### Bedrock Clients

For detected Bedrock players, UltimateShop determines whether to use Form based on `bedrock.enabled` and global `menu.bedrock.enabled`.

Bedrock Form is selected separately and does not participate in the Java client presentation priority.

### Default Values

If a menu does not explicitly define these settings:

| Menu Setting | Default Value |
| ----------------- | ------------- |
| `dialog.enabled` | `true` |
| `bedrock.enabled` | `true` |
| `arcmenu.enabled` | `false` |

These defaults do not guarantee that a presentation will be used. Global settings and runtime requirements must also be satisfied.

## Button & Product Configuration

In addition to menu-level settings, UltimateShop allows individual buttons and products to define presentation-specific behavior.

### Presentation Visibility

Use `menu-visibility` to control which presentations can display a button or product.

For example:

```
buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: EMERALD
name: '&aExample'

menu-visibility:
inventory: true
form: true
dialog: true
item-action-list: false
ore: false
arcmenu: true
```

| Option | Presentation |
| ------------------ | ---------------- |
| `inventory` | Inventory |
| `form` | Bedrock Form |
| `dialog` | Native Dialog |
| `item-action-list` | Dialog item list |
| `ore` | Ore |
| `arcmenu` | ArcMenu |

All options default to visible.

For `ore` and `item-action-list`, if their visibility is not explicitly configured, they inherit the value of `menu-visibility.dialog`.

For example:

```
menu-visibility:
dialog: false
ore: true
```

This hides the entry in native Dialog and Item Action List while allowing it to appear in Ore.

### Product Graphical Settings

Ore and ArcMenu allow individual products to override graphical settings.

For example, inside a shop file:

```
items:
A:
ui:
price:
enabled: false

actions:
primary:
- buy
```

For supported product-level settings such as `ui.price` and `ui.actions`, the lookup priority is:

**Product `ui.*` → Menu `ui.products.*` → Global `menu.ui.products.*` → Default Value**

These settings only affect graphical product presentation in Ore and ArcMenu. They do not change the action buttons of native Dialog or Bedrock Form.

### Graphical Element Placement

Ore and ArcMenu use `ui.placement` to determine the graphical position of buttons and products.

For example:

```
buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: EMERALD
name: '&aExample'

ui:
appearance: button

placement:
area: sidebar
order: 0
```

The `ui.placement` section references areas defined in the menu's `ui.layout.areas`.

Products can also inherit a default graphical placement from the menu's `ui.products.placement`.

Note that `menu-visibility` controls whether an entry is allowed to appear in a particular presentation, while `ui.placement` determines how it is positioned in graphical interfaces.

These settings serve different purposes and do not replace one another.

## Configuration Reference

The following table summarizes common menu settings and their locations.

| Configuration | YAML Path |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| Menu title | `title` |
| Menu content | `content` |
| Inventory size | `size` |
| Inventory slot layout | `layout` |
| Menu buttons | `buttons` |
| Menu opening conditions | `conditions` |
| Menu opening actions | `open-actions` |
| Menu closing actions | `close-actions` |
| Dynamic layout | `dynamic-layout` |
| Dialog settings | `dialog` |
| Bedrock Form settings | `bedrock` |
| ArcMenu settings | `arcmenu` |
| Graphical canvas and areas | `ui.layout` |
| Graphical product cards | `ui.products.card` |
| Graphical product prices | `ui.products.price` |
| Graphical product actions | `ui.products.actions` |
| Graphical theme colors | `ui.theme` |
| Graphical text | `ui.text` |
| Ore graphical templates | `ui.renderers.ore` |
| ArcMenu rendering settings | `ui.renderers.arcmenu` |
| Button or product visibility | `menu-visibility` |
| Button or product graphical placement | `ui.placement` |
| Button Dialog presentation options | `dialog.show-sprite`, `dialog.layout` |
| Bedrock Form icons and additional text | `display-item.bedrock` |
| Shop menu template | `settings.menu` |
| Shop-specific menu overrides | `settings.menu-settings` |

# Menu System

Menus are the screens players open. **Menu type** controls which data a screen shows; **presentation** controls how it looks. You can change the presentation without rewriting products or trade rules.

### Menu Types

All paths below are relative to `plugins/UltimateShop/`.

| Feature | File or configuration | Guide |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Navigation and custom buttons | `menus/common_menus/.yml` | [🔲 Common](/menu-types/general-menus.md) |
| Shop product list | `shops/.yml` + `menus/shop_menu_templates/.yml` | [🛍️ Shop](/menu-types/shop-menus.md) |
| Quantity selection | `menus/buy_more_menus/.yml` | [🔽 Buy More](/menu-types/buy-more-menus.md) |
| Search | `menus/search_menus/.yml` | [🔍 Search - Premium](/menu-types/search-menus-premium.md) |
| Favourite products | `menus/favourite_menus/.yml` | [❤️ Favourite - Premium](/menu-types/favourite-menus-premium.md) |
| Deposit items to sell | `menus/item_sell_menus/.yml` | [💰 Item Sell](/menu-types/item-sell-menus.md) |
| Sell all inventory items | `config.yml` → `menu.sell-all` | [🛒 Sell All](/menu-types/sell-all-menu.md) |

Please note:

* Search and Favourite require **Premium**.
* Shop-menu *templates* contain screen layout and ordinary buttons; shop files contain product prices and trading rules.
* Keep a menu ID unique among menus.

### Presentations

| Java client | Bedrock client |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [📦 Inventory](/menu-ui-modes/inventory-ui.md), [💬 Dialog - Premium](/menu-ui-modes/dialog-menus-premium.md), [🪨 Ore - Premium](/menu-ui-modes/ore-menus-premium.md), [✨ ArcMenu - Premium](/menu-ui-modes/arcmenu-menus-premium.md) | [🛏️ Form - Premium](/menu-ui-modes/bedrock-menus-premium.md) or Inventory |

See [presentation priority](/menu-ui-modes/ui-overview.md).

## First working example

Create `plugins/UltimateShop/menus/common_menus/hello.yml`:

```yaml
title: '&8Hello'
size: 9
layout:
- '0000A0000'
buttons:
A:
display-item:
material: EMERALD
name: '&aOpen main menu'
actions:
1:
type: open_menu
menu: main
```

Run `/shop reload`, then `/shop menu hello`. The target `main` menu must exist. `0` is an empty slot **unless** you define `buttons.0`.
